black-race.name: raza negra

blue-race.name: raza azul

bon.name: Bon

bosom-of-the-father.name: seno del Padre

backcheck.reading: The bosom of the Spirit, a close relation with the Holy Spirit.

bosora.name: Bosora

brahma.name: Brahma

brenner-pass.name: paso del Brennero

bretons.name: bretones

The reader must take it as "one who brings to completion", not "consumidor" (consumer).

second.name: Consumador del Destino del Universo
second.meaning: The unrevealed third member of the Trinity Absolute, with God the Supreme and God the Ultimate, whose act probably consummates destiny (0:12.7, 106:7.3).

backcheck.reading: Universe Destiny Consummator, one who brings destiny to completion.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree and the blind reader took it as 'one who brings destiny to completion' (106:7.3). 'universal' is kept for the English 'universal'.

contact-personalities.name: personalidades de contacto
contact-personalities.meaning: The few (fewer than a score) reservists who are conscious of their role as points of contact between superhuman beings and mortals, and the midwayers who serve these contacts (114:7.8, 77:8.8).

rejected.reason: Reads as an office 'contact person'; and 'person' is a different English word.

continence-cult.name: culto de la continencia
continence-cult.meaning: A cult of sexual renunciation that began among soldiers before battle, later practiced by 'saints', and that influenced Paul (89:3.6).

rejected.reason: 'Abstinencia' also covers food and drink.

backcheck.reading: A cult or religious practice based on sexual abstinence.
backcheck.note: Reading gives a cult based on sexual abstinence.

continental-nation.name: nación continental
continental-nation.meaning: The advanced nation on a neighboring planet of Satania that occupies one continent and whose government and society Paper 72 describes (72:0, 72:2.1, 72:12.2).

backcheck.reading: A nation that covers a whole continent.
misreadings: A mainland nation, not an island one.
backcheck.note: Reading gives a nation that covers a continent.

control-and-overcontrol.name: control y supercontrol
control-and-overcontrol.meaning: The relation of control on one level and the control from a higher level above it, as the time-space overcontrol of the Supreme over the domain of power (42:2.14).

rejected.reason: Would break the done form 'overcontrol: supercontrol'.

Problem in the earlier choice: the papers also use 'supercontrol' as a separate word (10:3.19, 'three supercontrols' of the Infinite Spirit), so 'supercontrol' now stands for two English words. 'sobrecontrol' for 'overcontrol' would keep them apart.

control-and-overcontrol.note: The done form 'overcontrol: supercontrol' clashes with the English word 'supercontrol' (10:3.19). A human must decide whether to change 'overcontrol' to 'sobrecontrol'.

backcheck.reading: Control and a higher control over it.
backcheck.note: Reading gives control and a higher control over it.

second.name: control y supercontrol
second.meaning: The two ways the papers describe how a higher power directs a lower level: direct control by the local controller or director, and overcontrol, the superior oversight of the Supreme, the Ultimate, or the First Source (42:2.14, 118:2.4, 1:2.10).

adjudicated.reason: The form follows the done term 'overcontrol: supercontrol', and both translators agree. The clash with the English word 'supercontrol' (10:3.19) is real; a human must decide whether 'overcontrol' and this term move to 'sobrecontrol' together.

corinth.name: Corinto
corinth.meaning: The capital of the Roman province of Achaia, visited by Jesus on his return from Rome (133:2.5).

backcheck.reading: Corinth, the Greek city of Paul's letters.

cornelius.name: Cornelio
cornelius.meaning: A Roman centurion of Caesarea who became a believer through Peter and whose steward was Anaxand (130:2.5).

backcheck.reading: Cornelius, a Roman centurion in Acts.

corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.name: personal corpóreo de los Príncipes Planetarios
corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.meaning: The one hundred ascendant volunteers who came with a Planetary Prince in material bodies as his visible helpers; on Urantia they were Caligastia's staff (77:1.2, 77:2.2, 66:4.10).

rejected.reason: The terms already done use "cuerpo" for "staff" (Van, del cuerpo del Príncipe), but "cuerpo corpóreo" repeats itself and "cuerpo" also means the body. "personal" avoids it.
Military sense.

corporeal-staffs-of-planetary-princes.note: Conflict with the earlier term "Van (del cuerpo del Príncipe)", where staff = "cuerpo". A human must decide which word "staff" takes everywhere.

decision.note: Consistency review 2026-10-21. Not yet checked by a Spanish speaker.

corporeality-error.name: error de la corporeidad
corporeality-error.meaning: The error of tying personality to a material body, seen in materialism (no body, no person after death) and in pantheism (God has no body, so is not a person) (1:5.12).

rejected.reason: 'Corporalidad' is less usual in philosophy than 'corporeidad'.
Reads as an error of the body, not an error about the body.

backcheck.reading: The error of believing that something spiritual has a body.
backcheck.note: Reading gives an error that ties the spiritual to a body.

corps-of-conjoint-trinitized-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trinitizados Conjuntos
corps-of-conjoint-trinitized-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven finaliter corps, located on Vicegerington, into which Havona natives are also received (31:1.5, 30:2.135).

rejected.reason: Decides that 'conjoint' modifies 'trinitized'; the English leaves it open.
Coins a new word and also closes the reading.

forcedChoices: Spanish agreement makes 'Conjuntos' grammatically modify 'Finalitarios'. A reader can still take it as 'jointly trinitized'; the done term 'Creador Conjunto' supports 'Conjunto' for 'Conjoint'.

second.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trinitizados Conjuntos
second.meaning: One of the seven finaliter corps, with headquarters on Vicegerington, into which Havona natives are also received (31:1.5, 31:10.5).

backcheck.reading: Corps of Co-ordinate Trinitized Finaliters, a group of final-state beings.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'Conjuntamente Trinitizados' would close the reading that the English leaves open, and 'Conjunto' matches the other 'Conjoint' terms.

corps-of-havona-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios de Havona
corps-of-havona-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven finaliter corps, a possible supreme destiny for Havona natives (31:1.5, 30:2.136).

corps-of-light-and-life.name: Cuerpo de Luz y Vida
corps-of-light-and-life.meaning: The corps on Paradise in which the ascendant mortals of time now serve temporarily; their final destiny is not known (31:3.2).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de la Luz y la Vida
rejected.reason: "light and life" is already "luz y vida" without articles.

second.name: Cuerpo de Luz y Vida
second.meaning: The Paradise corps in which the ascendant mortals of time serve for a time, while their finality destiny is unknown (31:3.2).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; 'luz y vida' is the fixed form without articles.

corps-of-mortal-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Mortales
corps-of-mortal-finaliters.meaning: The corps that is the present known destination of the ascending Adjuster-fused mortals, with other groups also assigned to it (31:0.1, 107:2.7).

rejected.reason: Kept as the alias for 'Corps of the Finality' because it pairs with 'finalitario', but Spanish 'finalidad' usually means 'purpose', not 'final state'. A human reviewer must decide; an alternative is 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'.

decision.note: "finalidad" reads as "purpose"; "Finality" follows "finalitarios"

corps-of-paradise-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Paradisíacos
corps-of-paradise-finaliters.meaning: The second of the seven finaliter corps in the Uversa register (30:2.133, 31:10.3).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
rejected.reason: Kept for the general 'Paradise Corps of the Finality'.
Breaks the pattern 'Paradise X' = 'X del Paraíso' in the done terms.
replaced by a human decision

corps-of-paradise-finaliters.note: The English aliases for this term list 'Paradise Corps of the Finality' and 'finaliter corps', but the papers use those for all seven corps (22:8.6). The papers name this corps only in two lists, so its exact membership is implied, not stated.

decision.note: Consistency review 2026-10-21. Not yet checked by a Spanish speaker.

corps-of-perfection.name: Cuerpo de Perfección
corps-of-perfection.meaning: The local universe corps that Spirit-fused ascenders, who never become finaliters, finally join (37:5.3, 37:5.4).

rejected.reason: Possible, but the done terms use "de Perfección" without the article (Hijos Trinitizados de Perfección).

corps-of-permanent-citizens.name: cuerpo de ciudadanos permanentes
corps-of-permanent-citizens.meaning: The resident orders of beings who form the stable population of administrative worlds, such as the Material Sons on Jerusem and the susatia on Salvington (37:9.7, 37:9.12, 76:6.3).

corps-of-seraphic-completion.name: Cuerpo de Culminación Seráfica
corps-of-seraphic-completion.meaning: The corps of seraphim who traversed the circles of Seraphington, attained Paradise, and received the embrace of the Eternal Son (39:9.1).

rejected.reason: exists but is rare and stiff
suggests an ending or a stop, not an attainment

second.name: Cuerpo de Culminación Seráfica
second.meaning: The angels who have traversed Seraphington, attained Paradise and the embrace of the Eternal Son, and now serve with seconaphim and supernaphim (39:9.1, 39:1.5, 113:7.5).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'Culminación' gives attainment, as in 'Cuerpo de Culminación de Nebadon'; 'Terminación' suggests a stop.

decision.note: "finalidad" reads as "purpose"; "Finality" follows "finalitarios"

corps-of-transcendental-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trascendentales
corps-of-transcendental-finaliters.meaning: One of the seven Paradise finaliter corps, the corps related to transcendental service, to which Havona natives are also admitted (31:0, 31:8).

second.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trascendentales
second.meaning: One of the finaliter corps, on Paradise, which receives Havona natives as one of their supreme destinies (31:1.5, 30:2.137).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree and the judge matched; the form follows the other finaliter corps.

corps-of-trinitized-finaliters.name: Cuerpo de Finalitarios Trinitizados
corps-of-trinitized-finaliters.meaning: The finality corps that appears to be the supreme destiny of most creature-trinitized sons, one of the seven Paradise Corps of the Finality (22:8.6, 26:11.2).

rejected.reason: The article is not in the English and breaks the pattern of 'Cuerpo de Finalitarios Mortales'.

corps-of-unrevealed-sons-of-destiny.name: Cuerpo de Hijos del Destino No Revelados
corps-of-unrevealed-sons-of-destiny.meaning: The seventh of the finaliter corps, whose nature the papers do not reveal (31:10.8, 30:2.138).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de Hijos No Revelados del Destino
rejected.reason: Splits "Hijos del Destino"; the agreement of "No Revelados" with "Hijos" already shows what is unrevealed.

forcedChoices: "No Revelados" must agree in gender and number; it agrees with "Hijos", which is the reading of the English.

second.name: Cuerpo de Hijos no Revelados del Destino
second.meaning: The seventh of the finaliter corps, whose nature and work are not revealed (31:10.8, 30:2.138).

backcheck.reading: Corps of Unrevealed Sons of Destiny.

adjudicated.reason: The seventh finaliter corps (31:10.8). This keeps 'Hijos del Destino' together and puts 'No Revelados' on the Sons, as in 'Centros No Clasificados'.

correctional-rest.name: descanso correctivo
correctional-rest.meaning: The rest that follows the instruction a Melchizedek receives from the Creator Son after an error of judgment, before reinstatement on the third day (35:2.8).

rejected.reason: 'Correccional' reads as a prison (correctional facility).
Adds a sense of punishment that the text does not state.

backcheck.reading: A rest that corrects or heals something.
misreadings: A rehabilitation pause in medicine or prison.
backcheck.note: Reading gives a rest that corrects; context completes it.

cosmic-citizenship.name: ciudadanía cósmica
cosmic-citizenship.meaning: The recognition of one's obligations to the Supreme Being and membership in the universe community, which gives security on the way to Paradise (118:6.8).

rejected.reason: Reads as world citizenship, a political idea.

backcheck.reading: Citizenship of the universe, belonging to the whole cosmos.
misreadings: A New Age or esoteric idea.
backcheck.note: Reading gives citizenship of the universe.

cosmic-cloud.name: nube cósmica
cosmic-cloud.meaning: The great space blanket of Orvonton, made mostly of modified calcium atoms, the pulverized stone that is building matter for planets (41:6.2, 57:8.22).

rejected.reason: 'Nebulosa' translates 'nebulae' in the glossary.

backcheck.reading: A cloud in space, made of gas or dust.
backcheck.note: Reading gives a cloud of gas or dust in space.

cosmic-consciousness.name: conciencia cósmica
cosmic-consciousness.meaning: Awareness of the realities of the universe beyond the material and local outlook; the term itself is not defined in the papers.

rejected.reason: Also valid; 'conciencia' is the more common spelling across Latin America.
The reader must not bring this; the sense is awareness.

second.name: conciencia cósmica
second.meaning: Awareness of the universe as a whole, which implies the recognition of a First Cause and is born in earnest on the fifth mansion world (0:2.2, 0:0.2, 47:7.5, 104:3.2).

adjudicated.reason: Awareness of the universe that recognizes a First Cause (0:2.2, 47:7.5). The plain form is correct, and context removes the New Age sense.

cosmic-force.name: fuerza cósmica
cosmic-force.meaning: The pre-energy form of space potency, the first stage of its individuation (11:8.5, 42:2).

backcheck.reading: A force present in the whole universe.
misreadings: A New Age or esoteric energy.
backcheck.note: Reading gives a force in the whole universe.

cosmic-mind.name: mente cósmica
cosmic-mind.meaning: The sevenfold mind of time and space, a subabsolute manifestation of the mind of the Third Source and Center, ministered by the Seven Master Spirits to the superuniverses (0:6.1, 16:6).

rejected.reason: Collides with 'Universal Mind' (Mente Universal).

second.name: mente cósmica
second.meaning: The sevenfold mind of time and space, the intellectual potential of the grand universe, ministered by the Seven Master Spirits as a subabsolute manifestation of the mind of the Third Source and Center (16:6.1, 56:2.3, 9:6.6).

cosmic-reserve-corps.name: cuerpo de reserva cósmico
cosmic-reserve-corps.meaning: A group of more than one thousand universe-conscious mortals on Urantia whose insight of cosmic citizenship transcends their world; their function is not revealed (114:7.13).

rejected.reason: 'Cuerpo de reserva' is already a fixed unit in 'cuerpo de reserva del destino'.

backcheck.reading: A reserve body or group kept for use across the universe.
backcheck.note: Reading gives a reserve group kept for universe use.

cosmos-infinite.name: cosmos-infinito
cosmos-infinite.meaning: The illimitable cosmos beyond the master universe, whose energy potential is present in Paradise and of which the grand and master universes are only partial manifestations (104:4.26).

rejected.reason: The hyphen of the English marks one coined name; it stays only as an alias.

backcheck.reading: A cosmos with no end, the universe seen as infinite.
backcheck.note: Reading gives the cosmos seen as infinite.

council-of-equilibrium.name: Consejo del Equilibrio
council-of-equilibrium.meaning: The high commissioners of power, sent by the Seven Master Spirits from the Associate Master Force Organizers, who direct the Master Physical Controllers and read the master frandalanks (29:4.2, 57:1.4).

backcheck.reading: Council of Equilibrium, a being or body that balances.

council-of-perfection.name: consejo de perfección
council-of-perfection.meaning: A council on Paradise to which superuniverse conciliators are translated, and from which they emerge as a co-ordinating corps of the Infinite Spirit (25:3.16).

rejected.reason: The English has no article; the article would suggest an abstract named Perfection.

second.name: consejo de perfección
second.meaning: The council on Paradise to which superuniverse conciliators are translated and from which they emerge as the co-ordinating corps of the Infinite Spirit; the papers also call the supreme tribunals 'councils of perfection' (25:3.16, 15:12.3).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. The English has no article, and an article would suggest a named abstract Perfection.

council-of-planetary-princes.name: consejo de los Príncipes Planetarios
aliases: consejo de sistema de los gobernantes de mundos
council-of-planetary-princes.meaning: The system council of world rulers, the Planetary Princes and resident governors general, over which the System Sovereign presides at the system headquarters (45:2.4, 114:3.4).

council-of-seven.name: consejo de siete
council-of-seven.meaning: The council of the red man, after the teaching of Onamonalonton, whose rule was unanimous (70:5.4).

rejected.reason: Suggests seven known persons, which the English does not say.

second.name: consejo de los siete
second.meaning: The tribal government of certain red-race tribes that kept Onamonalonton's teaching and ruled by the unanimous vote of seven (70:5.4).

adjudicated.reason: A tribal council of seven members that ruled by unanimous vote (70:5.4). 'De los siete' implies a known group of seven.

council-of-seventy.name: consejo de setenta
council-of-seventy.meaning: A council at the constellation headquarters, selected from evolutionary beings, analogous to the twenty-four counselors (50:2.2).

rejected.reason: Can be confused with "the seventy" messengers of Jesus' time.

second.name: consejo de los setenta
second.meaning: A council at the constellation headquarters, selected from the evolutionary beings of the realms, analogous to the four and twenty counselors of the system (50:2.2).

adjudicated.reason: A council at the constellation headquarters (50:2.2). 'De los setenta' calls up the biblical Seventy, which is not the meaning here.

council-on-food-and-material-welfare.name: consejo de alimentación y bienestar material
council-on-food-and-material-welfare.meaning: The first council of the Caligastia one hundred, led by Ang, which fostered food, water, clothes, and material advance (66:5.2).

backcheck.reading: Council of food and material welfare.

counseling-the-rich-man.name: consejos al hombre rico
counseling-the-rich-man.meaning: Jesus' advice in Rome to a wealthy Roman citizen and Stoic on how to acquire and use wealth as a trust (132:5).

rejected.reason: Reads as a paid financial service.

backcheck.reading: The advice that Jesus gave to the rich young man.
misreadings: Financial advice to a wealthy person.
backcheck.note: Reading names the Gospel rich young man, not the Roman citizen of 132:5.

adjudicated.reason: 132:5 shows Jesus give a Roman Stoic citizen many counsels on wealth over several conferences, so the plural fits. It stays apart from 'joven rico' and from 'hombre rico de Roma' in the glossary.

counselors-and-advisers.name: consejeros y asesores
counselors-and-advisers.meaning: The sixth order of secondary supernaphim, who counsel Paradise pilgrims and also comfort those who fail in their first effort at Deity attainment (26:4.8, 26:10.2).

rejected.reason: 'consultor' suggests a paid business consultant.

counselors-and-advisers.note: The same English phrase is used as plain words for the Unions of Days (18:6.1); there it is not the name of an order.

second.name: consejeros y asesores
second.meaning: Secondary supernaphim of the second Havona circle who instruct ascenders on the eternal career and comfort those who failed in the first effort at Deity attainment (26:4.8, 26:10.2).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'asesores' is the glossary form for 'advisers' (Technical Advisers), and 'consultores' suggests a business consultant.

counting-the-cost.name: calcular el costo
counting-the-cost.meaning: Jesus' teaching at the ford near Bethany that a disciple must weigh what discipleship costs, up to family and life, before he begins (171:2).

rejected.reason: Too literal; 'contar' also means 'to tell'.
'Coste' is mainly used in Spain; 'costo' is understood everywhere.

backcheck.reading: To calculate the cost before one starts something (Luke 14:28).
backcheck.note: Reading gives the Luke 14 teaching on the cost before one starts.

court-advisers.name: asesores de los tribunales
court-advisers.meaning: Supreme seraphim attached to all orders of adjudication who see that charges against mortals are stated in justice and adjudicated in mercy, often as defenders of mortals (39:1.7, 39:1.8).

rejected.reason: 'corte' also means a royal court, a sense the English does not intend.
'consejero' is the glossary form for 'counselor', and 'adviser' is 'asesor' (counselors and advisers: consejeros y asesores).

court-of-gentiles.name: atrio de los gentiles
court-of-gentiles.meaning: The outer court of the Jerusalem temple open to gentiles (125:4.3, 162:4.3).

rejected.reason: 'corte' is a royal or judicial court.

backcheck.reading: Court of the Gentiles in the Jerusalem temple.

court-of-israel.name: atrio de Israel
court-of-israel.meaning: A court of the Jerusalem temple from which steps led down to the court of the women (162:4.3).

backcheck.reading: Court of Israel in the temple.

court-of-priests.name: atrio de los sacerdotes
court-of-priests.meaning: The court of the Jerusalem temple, below the rock ledge in front of the temple, where the altar stood and sacrifices were made (125:1.4, 162:4.4).

rejected.reason: "corte" means a royal court or a law court, not an open area of a building.

backcheck.reading: Court of the priests in the temple.

court-of-women.name: atrio de las mujeres
court-of-women.meaning: The court of the Jerusalem temple below the court of Israel, lit by great candelabras at the feast of tabernacles, where John made his Nazarite cleansing sacrifices (162:4.2, 162:4.3, 135:2.1).

rejected.reason: False friend: 'corte' is a royal court or a tribunal, not an enclosed yard.
Correct but domestic; 'atrio' is the usual word for the courts of the temple.

court-of-women.note: Translators must use 'atrio' for the other temple courts too (court of Israel, court of the gentiles) so the set stays consistent.

second.name: atrio de las mujeres
second.meaning: The court of the Jerusalem temple below the court of Israel, where the great candelabras burned at the Feast of Tabernacles (162:4.2, 162:4.3).

backcheck.reading: Court of the women in the temple.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'atrio' is the form for every temple court in the glossary (atrio de Israel, de los gentiles, de los sacerdotes).

courtesy-colonies.name: colonias de cortesía
courtesy-colonies.meaning: Groups of visiting beings who reside on headquarters worlds by courtesy, such as star students, celestial artisans, and reversion directors (46:5.30, 18:5.2, 37:10).

rejected.reason: Interprets the term instead of keeping the English word 'courtesy'.

second.name: colonias de cortesía
second.meaning: Seven groups of beings (star students, celestial artisans, reversion directors, and others) who sojourn on the architectural spheres while they carry out their missions (30:3.1, 46:5.30, 18:5.2).

misreadings: Courtesy as politeness, or colonies as political territories

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree and the judge matched. The form keeps the English word 'courtesy' without commentary.

crab-nebula.name: nebulosa del Cangrejo
crab-nebula.meaning: An irregular nebula that began about nine hundred years ago, with its mother sphere still a lone star near its center (41:8.4).

craftworkers-of-color.name: artífices del color
craftworkers-of-color.meaning: Designers and embellishers among the celestial artisans who make the ten thousand color tones of spirit reflection give out messages of harmonious beauty (44:6.3).

rejected.reason: "artisans" is already "artesanos"; "craftworkers" needs a different word.

second.name: artífices del color
second.meaning: Designers and embellishers among the celestial artisans who make the ten thousand color tones of spirit reflection sound out their messages of beauty (44:6.3).

backcheck.reading: Color artisans, those who craft color.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'artesanos' is fixed for 'artisans', so 'artífices' keeps the two English words apart.

creative-daughters.name: Hijas Creativas
creative-daughters.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirits, in whom the Infinite Spirit serves the ascension of material creatures, partners of the Creator Sons (8:4.4, 104:2.3).

rejected.reason: 'Creative Mother Spirits' is already 'Espíritus Madre Creativos'; the family uses 'Creativ-'.

backcheck.reading: Creative Daughters, female beings who create.

creative-mother-spirits.name: Espíritus Madre Creativos
creative-mother-spirits.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirits seen in their creative partnership with the Creator Sons (Paper 34, 39:1.2 'Creative Spirit').

rejected.reason: 'Creadores' is fixed for 'Creator' (Hijos Creadores); 'Creative' is a different English word.
The reader must not bring the artistic or marketing sense; it means 'creating'.

second.name: Espíritus Madre Creativos
second.meaning: The local universe personalizations of the Infinite Spirit, the creative partners of the Creator Sons, known in Satania as the Divine Minister (34:1.4, 25:2.4, 34:5.6).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'Creadores' is fixed for 'Creator', and 'Creativos' matches 'Hijas Creativas' and 'Espíritus Creativos'.

creative-spirits.name: Espíritus Creativos
creative-spirits.meaning: The local universe Mother Spirits, Creative Daughters of the Infinite Spirit, who create and administer with the Creator Sons (8:5.3, 39:1.2).

rejected.reason: Merges 'Creative' with 'Creator'; the papers keep the two words apart.

second.name: Espíritus Creativos
second.meaning: The local universe Spirits produced by the Infinite Spirit each time a Creator Son is brought forth; what the Infinite Spirit is to all creation, a Creative Spirit is to a local universe (9:8.4, 9:8.5).

misreadings: Spirits in the sense of ghosts

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. The papers keep 'Creative' apart from 'Creator', and the glossary does the same.

creator-sons.name: Hijos Creadores
creator-sons.meaning: The makers and rulers of the local universes, Paradise Sons of the order of Michael, born of the Father and the Eternal Son (21:0.1, 32:0.1).

rejected.reason: 'Michael' is here the name of an order of Sons; the Spanish name 'Miguel' brings in the archangel and a common personal name. See michael-of-nebadon.

second.name: Hijos Creadores
second.meaning: The makers and rulers of the local universes, of dual origin in the Father and the Eternal Son, each unique (21:0.1, 0:8.11).

misreadings: Christian sense of the Son of God as creator

adjudicated.reason: Consistency review: The decided form is Miguel / Migueles.

creatorship.name: condición de creador
creatorship.meaning: Not one attribute of God but the aggregate of his acting nature, the universal function of creating, which culminates in the Fatherhood of God (3:0.3).

rejected.reason: Means a human talent for new ideas.
Not a Spanish word; reads as a coinage that the English does not need.
Good in 3:0.3, but the papers also use 'creatorship charge' as a commission, where 'función' fails.

creatorship.note: Spanish has no single noun for 'creatorship'. A human must decide if a phrase is acceptable in all uses (3:0.3, 17:6.5 'creatorship charge').

backcheck.reading: The state or rank of being a creator.
misreadings: A condition imposed by an author (contract sense).

mount-assembly.name: Monte de la Asamblea

mount-carmel.name: monte Carmelo
mount-carmel.meaning: The long ridge in northwest Palestine running down to the sea, linked with Elijah's story against the priests of Baal (123:5.12, 128:3.2).

mount-gerizim.name: monte Gerizim

mount-gilboa.name: monte Gilboa

mount-hermon.name: monte Hermón

mount-hood.name: monte Hood
mount-hood.meaning: A mountain of western North America that began its mountain career about 10,000,000 years ago (61:4.2).

mount-of-olives.name: monte de los Olivos
mount-of-olives.meaning: The hill east of Jerusalem on whose eastern slopes Bethany lay (124:6.9).

mount-of-transfiguration.name: monte de la transfiguración

mount-olivet.name: monte de los Olivos

mount-olympus.name: monte Olimpo
mount-olympus.meaning: The home of the happy-go-lucky Greek gods, more human than divine, whom the intelligent Greeks never took very seriously (98:1.4).

mount-rainier.name: monte Rainier
mount-rainier.meaning: A mountain of western North America that began its mountain career about 10,000,000 years ago (61:4.2).

mount-royal.name: monte Royal

mount-sartaba.name: monte Sartaba
mount-sartaba.meaning: The highest mountain over the Jordan valley, crowned by the Alexandrian fortress where Herod imprisoned a wife and buried two strangled sons (124:6.6, 122:7.6).

mount-seraph.name: Monte Serafín
mount-seraph.meaning: The highest elevation on Jerusem, the point of departure for all transport seraphim (46:2.8).

mount-shasta.name: monte Shasta
mount-shasta.meaning: A mountain of western North America that began its mountain career about 10,000,000 years ago (61:4.2).

mount-sinai.name: monte Sinaí
mount-sinai.meaning: The volcano (Mount Horeb) associated with Yahweh by the southern tribes, and a source of iron ore (96:1.3, 80:6.3).

mount-tabor.name: monte Tabor
mount-tabor.meaning: The mountain range east of Nazareth whose summit Jesus first climbed with Joseph at nine (122:6.1, 124:1.6).

mystery-monitors.name: Monitores de Misterio
mystery-monitors.meaning: Another name of the Thought Adjusters, the divine fragments of the Father that indwell mortal minds (Paper 107).

mysticism.name: misticismo

nabal.name: Nabal
nabal.meaning: A rich Edomite whose widow David married to build himself up politically (97:9.10).

nabodad.name: Nabodad

nabon.name: Nabon

naboths.name: los Nabot

nabu.name: Nabú

nahor-old-testament.name: Nacor (Antiguo Testamento)

second.name: Nacor (Antiguo Testamento)

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'Nacor' is the widespread Spanish form; the qualifier keeps him apart from the rabbi and the evangelist.

nahor-rabbi.name: Nacor (rabino)

adjudicated.reason: The form follows the base 'Nacor', and the qualifier keeps the Jerusalem teacher (123:6.8) apart from the evangelist (150:9.3).

nain.name: Naín

nalda.name: Nalda
nalda.meaning: The woman of Sychar at Jacob's well to whom Jesus offered the living water (143:5.2, 143:5.4).

nambia.name: Nambia

nanak-guru.name: Nanak, Gurú
nanak-guru.meaning: Guru Nanak, the religious leader who closes the papers' list 'from Onagar to Guru Nanak' (92:5.8).

naomi.name: Noemí

naples.name: Nápoles
naples.meaning: The Italian port city where Jesus, Gonod, and Ganid stayed on the way to Rome (130:0.2, 130:8.4).

nasanta.name: Nasanta
nasanta.meaning: Daughter of Elman the Syrian physician, one of the ten women commissioned by Jesus (150:1.1).

nathan-of-busiris.name: Natán de Busiris

nathan-of-caesarea.name: Natán de Cesarea

nathan-of-cana.name: Natán de Caná

nathan-of-nazareth.name: Natán de Nazaret

nathaniel-apostle.name: Natanael (apóstol)

nathaniel-the-pharisee.name: Natanael el fariseo
nathaniel-the-pharisee.meaning: A wealthy Pharisee of Ragaba who gave a Sabbath breakfast for about twenty Pharisees with Jesus as guest of honor (166:1.1, 166:1.2).

national-council-of-defense.name: Consejo Nacional de Defensa
national-council-of-defense.meaning: On a neighboring planet, the council of twenty-five members that commissions 'guardians of civilization' and in war can assess the states for money, men, and materials (72:11.1, 72:7.7).

nazareth.name: Nazaret
nazareth.meaning: The town in Galilee where Jesus grew up (Papers 122-126).

nazarites.name: nazareos

neanderthalers.name: neandertales

nebadon.name: Nebadon

nebuchadnezzar.name: Nabucodonosor

nereids.name: Nereidas

nerites.name: Neritas

new-red-sandstone.name: Nueva Arenisca Roja

nod-prince-s-corporeal-staff.name: Nod (del personal corpóreo del Príncipe)
nod-prince-s-corporeal-staff.meaning: The leader of the Dalamatia commission on industry and trade among the Prince's staff, first leader of the rebels, from whom the Nodites take their name (66:5.11, 73:1.3).

rejected.reason: Matches the earlier "Van (del cuerpo del Príncipe)", but "cuerpo" can read as the Prince's physical body; "personal corpóreo" follows the done term "corporeal staffs of Planetary Princes".

nod-prince-s-corporeal-staff.note: The terms already done use two forms for "Prince's staff": "personal corpóreo" and "cuerpo" (Van). A reviewer must unify them.

second.name: Nod (del personal corpóreo del Príncipe)
second.meaning: The onetime chairman of the Dalamatia commission on industry and trade, first leader of the rebel staff members whose descendants are the Nodites (73:1.3, 77:3.1).

backcheck.reading: Nod, a member of the Prince's corporeal staff.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. The form follows the fixed root 'personal corpóreo' and the done 'personal corpóreo del Príncipe'; 'cuerpo' can read as a physical body.

nodites.name: Noditas
nodites.meaning: The descendants of the rebel members of Caligastia's staff, named after Nod, the eighth race on Urantia (73:1.3, 77:2.1).

nog.name: Nog
nog.meaning: The false god of light and fire to whom renegades of Dalamatia turned the Father's temple before the city was engulfed (67:5.5).

nonbreathers.name: no respiradores
nonbreathers.meaning: Mortals of worlds without air who do not breathe; one and one-half per cent of Satania worlds; they are candidates for Spirit fusion (49:2.14, 49:3.5).

rejected.reason: A biology term for organisms that live without oxygen; the papers make no such claim.
Not a natural Spanish form.

backcheck.note: Beings that do not breathe fits.

second.name: no respirantes
second.meaning: Mortals of worlds that have no air, such as a world like the moon; one of the planetary physical types, and candidates for Spirit fusion (49:2.14, 49:3.5).

adjudicated.reason: 49:2.14: mortals of airless worlds who do not breathe. It follows 'subrespiradores' and 'superrespiradores' in the glossary.

nonresistance.name: no resistencia
nonresistance.meaning: Jesus' teaching to overcome evil by good and not to resist evil with selfish reaction; he did not mean passive submission (143:1.2-3, 159:5, 140:8).

rejected.reason: The papers deny that nonresistance is passivity.
A modern political term, not the English idea.

backcheck.note: Same first guess as the English; the papers clarify it is not passive submission.

nonsurvivors.name: no supervivientes
nonsurvivors.meaning: Mortals who do not survive death because they reject eternal life; their personality ends, and the Adjuster keeps any surviving values (112:5, 117:4).

rejected.reason: See 'sleeping survivors': the family of 'supervivencia' decides.

backcheck.note: Those who do not survive fits.

norana.name: Norana
norana.meaning: The Syrian, Greek-speaking gentile woman whose persistent faith brought Jesus to heal her daughter (156:1.3, 156:1.5).

nordan-the-kenite.name: Nordan el quenita
nordan-the-kenite.meaning: A brilliant disciple of Melchizedek to whom, with his students, Melchizedek taught the truths of the superuniverse and of Havona (93:3.4).

nordic-race.name: raza nórdica
nordic-race.meaning: The 'so-called' northern white race, mostly of the blue man and the Andite (80:9.2).

norlatiadek.name: Norlatiadek
norlatiadek.meaning: Constellation number seventy of Nebadon, with one hundred local systems including Satania and its headquarters on Edentia (15:14.6, 46:8.3).

north-america.name: América del Norte
north-america.meaning: The continent that the red man and later the Eskimos entered (64:7.18).

rejected.reason: Also correct; 'América del Norte' matches 'América del Sur' in the done list.

north-pole.name: Polo Norte
north-pole.meaning: The northern pole of the earth, which marine fossils reach (59:3.7).

north-sea.name: mar del Norte
north-sea.meaning: The sea toward whose then warm waters the descendants of Andon and Fonta made over one thousand settlements along the great rivers (63:5.2, 64:2.6, 61:5.8).

norway.name: Noruega
norway.meaning: The land of the Norwegian fiords down which great icebergs went into the North Sea in the ice age (61:5.8).

obadiah.name: Abdías
obadiah.meaning: The Hebrew prophet who, with Micah, followed the first Isaiah and attacked the sacrificial system (97:5.4).

oban.name: Oban
oban.meaning: The settlement near the present Caspian Sea where Onagar had his headquarters and from which he sent out the first missionaries (63:6.7).

observers-universe.name: observadores (del universo)
observers-universe.meaning: Agents commissioned by executive decree of a System Sovereign to represent the system to other systems and at the constellation capital, within the local universe only (33:6.4).

backcheck.reading: Observers of the universe, beings who watch it.
misreadings: Official observers or monitors at an event
backcheck.note: Observers is a fair first guess; context gives the envoy role.

og.name: Og
og.meaning: Og, the king of Bashan, whose land the Hebrews raided with brutal slaughter (69:8.3).

ohio.name: Ohio
ohio.meaning: The Ohio region and river in North America, named for coral deposits and as the southern limit of an ice sheet (59:4.6, 61:7.2).

ohio-river.name: río Ohio
ohio-river.meaning: The river whose banks near Louisville expose thick Devonian coral deposits (59:4.6).

okhban.name: Okhban
okhban.meaning: One of the four great prophets of Egypt, whom the Egyptians murdered (95:3.5).

old-testament.name: Antiguo Testamento
old-testament.meaning: The Hebrew scriptures, which Jesus treated as human writings that contain truth and error (159:4.1).

second.name: Antiguo Testamento
second.meaning: The Hebrew scriptures, whose so-called Messianic prophecies were applied to Jesus after his life (122:4.4).

oligocene.name: Oligoceno
oligocene.meaning: The geologic period, covering ten million years, by whose close most plant, marine, and land life was present much as today (61:2.13).

olivet.name: monte de los Olivos
olivet.meaning: Olivet, the hill east of Jerusalem with Bethany on its eastern slopes (124:6.9).

rejected.reason: Correct but rare; many readers do not know it. Kept as an alias.

olivet.note: Same form as 'Mount of Olives' and 'Mount Olivet', because the three name one place.

second.name: Olivete
second.meaning: The Mount of Olives east of Jerusalem, on whose brow Jesus first saw the city (124:6.10) and on whose eastern slope Bethany lies (124:6.9).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree on the place, and the form matches 'Mount of Olives' and 'Mount Olivet'. 'Olivete' stays as an alias because many readers do not know it.

olympian-religion.name: religión olímpica
olympian-religion.meaning: The Greek religion of the gods of Olympus, which promised no salvation and nearly vanished within a millennium (98:2.1).

omniaphim.name: omniafines
omniaphim.meaning: Ministering spirits of the superuniverses created by the Infinite Spirit with the Seven Supreme Executives, who are their exclusive servants and messengers in the oversight of the superuniverses (26:1.13, 28:2.1, 28:2.2).

rejected.reason: Keeps the Hebrew-style plural; the done list uses -afines (seconafines, supernafines).

omnificence.name: omnificencia
omnificence.meaning: The false idea that God personally does all that is done; God is omnipotent but not omnificent (118:6.1, 118:6.2, 118:6.8).

rejected.reason: The papers set the two apart.
Not a word; the Latin root gives 'omnificencia'.

omnificence.note: 'Omnificencia' is rare in Spanish; most readers can understand it only from the context (118:6.1).

backcheck.reading: Doing all good, or being all-beneficent.
backcheck.note: Read as all-beneficent, not as doing everything.

second.name: omnificencia
second.meaning: Omnificence is the false idea that God personally does everything that is done, which would take away the standing of all other persons and lead to pantheism; God is omnipotent but not omnificent (118:6.1, 118:6.8).

adjudicated.reason: 118:6.1 defines it: God 'does not personally do all that is done'. The English word is rare and the text defines it; a descriptive form would lose the pair with 'omnipotencia' in the section title. Medium confidence in the form.

omnipotent.name: Omnipotente
omnipotent.meaning: The name for God the Ultimate when he becomes manifest to the universes of time as the transcendental Almighty, with overcontrol of supertime and transcended space (118:2.4; 0:1.10).

rejected.reason: Already the form of 'Almighty' (Almighty Supreme, transcendental Almighty); 118:2.4 sets the two names side by side.

omri.name: Omri
omri.meaning: A king of Israel who tried to buy Shemer's estate in a time of land trading by city despots (97:9.18).

onagar.name: Onagar
onagar.meaning: The first truth teacher of early mankind, who led his fellows in the worship of "The Breath Giver" and now serves among the four and twenty counselors (63:6.7, 45:4.3).

onamonalonton.name: Onamonalonton
onamonalonton.meaning: A leader and spiritual deliverer of the red men about 65 000 years ago who turned them to the worship of the Great Spirit (64:6.7, 45:4.5).

one-brained-mortals.name: mortales de un cerebro
one-brained-mortals.meaning: Mortals of the one-brained type, the simplest of the three brain types of the inhabited worlds (49:5).

rejected.reason: A learned coinage; the English is a plain description.
'Solo' adds an emphasis that the English does not have.

second.name: mortales de un cerebro
second.meaning: Mortals of the first of three basic brain types, less imaginative than the two-brained and less spiritual than the three-brained, with the same destiny (49:5.13, 40:5.17).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it is a plain description, as in 49:5.

one-god.name: Dios Único
one-god.meaning: The title of Ikhnaton's book of thirty-one chapters, «The One God», which the priests destroyed; the title names the One God, creator of Aton (95:5.7).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'a god', an indefinite article, and loses the sense of the one and only God.
Natural, but stresses 'the only' as an adverb; 'Dios Único' reads better as a title.

one-god.note: In 95:5.7 the title carries the article: «The One God». A translator can write «El Dios Único» in the title.

second.name: Dios Único
second.meaning: The title of the book of thirty-one chapters by Ikhnaton, which the priests destroyed when they returned to power; also the One God whom he worshiped in disguise as creator of Aton (95:5.7).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. The form reads as a title; 'Un Dios' reads as 'a god'. A translator can add the article in the book title (95:5.7).

one-high-in-authority.name: Uno Elevado en Autoridad
one-high-in-authority.meaning: One member of the order Those High in Authority, who sits with a Mighty Messenger and One without Name and Number in an ascendant commission (19:3.7, 22:4.6).

rejected.reason: Must follow 'Aquellos Elevados en Autoridad'.

one-hundred-councils-of-supreme-sanction.name: cien consejos de sanción suprema
one-hundred-councils-of-supreme-sanction.meaning: The councils on Salvington whose presidents form Gabriel's working cabinet (33:8.4).

backcheck.reading: A hundred councils with supreme authority to sanction or approve.
misreadings: Councils that impose penalties (sanción as punishment)
backcheck.note: Councils with supreme authority to approve fits.

one-truth.name: Verdad Única
one-truth.meaning: The object of worship that Singlangton taught the yellow race about one hundred thousand years ago, one truth instead of many (64:6.15, 45:4.8).

rejected.reason: Reads as 'a truth' (indefinite), which loses the contrast with many.
Philosophical and unusual in plain Spanish.

second.name: Verdad Única
second.meaning: The one deity whose worship Singlangton proclaimed to the yellow race about one hundred thousand years ago, in place of many (64:6.15, 45:4.8, 79:8.4).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. The form keeps the contrast with many truths (64:6.15); 'Una Verdad' reads as 'a truth'.

one-uncaused.name: UNO INCAUSADO
one-uncaused.meaning: The First Source and Center as the only uncaused one, the primeval cause of causes (0:3.23, 118:6.2).

rejected.reason: Correct but reads as a participle, not a title.
Correct, but 'sin causa' also means 'for no reason'.

one-uncaused.note: 'incausado' is a philosophical word; check that general readers accept it.

second.name: UNO INCAUSADO
second.meaning: The one being that has no beginning, the primeval cause of causes, conceptualized as the I AM (0:3.23); 'one uncaused Cause' in 118:6.2.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'Incausado' reads as a title; 'sin causa' also means 'for no reason'.

one-without-name-and-number.name: Uno sin Nombre ni Número
one-without-name-and-number.meaning: One member of the order Those without Name and Number, part of the ascendant commission (19:3.7, 22:4.6).

backcheck.reading: The One without Name or Number.

ophel.name: Ofel
ophel.meaning: A district of Jerusalem through which the water procession of the feast of tabernacles passed on its way to the fountain gate near Siloam (162:4.4).

orange-race.name: raza anaranjada
orange-race.meaning: One of the six Sangik races; after a long struggle with the green men in Egypt it ceased to exist as a race about one hundred thousand years ago (64:6.13).

rejected.reason: Correct, but 'anaranjada' agrees in gender and reads better as an adjective.

ordovician.name: Ordovícico
ordovician.meaning: The geologists' name for the second great period of marine life (59:2.13).

original.name: Original
original.meaning: The I AM considered as the source reality that always is, in which the Actual and the Potential are both encircuited (115:3.11, 115:3.16, 0:3.22).

rejected.reason: The masculine reads as a person or as "the original copy" of a document.
Means "native of" or "derived from", which reverses the sense of a source.

forcedChoices: Spanish needs an article for the nominalized adjective; chose the neuter "lo" to match the done term "Actual, lo" and the triad Original, Actual, Potential (115:3.9).

second.name: Original
second.meaning: The unqualified concept of the First Source and Center, the source manifestation of the I AM from which all reality takes origin, set beside the Actual and the Potential (115:3.6).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. The neuter 'lo Original' matches the done 'Actual, lo' and the triad Original, Actual, Potential (115:3.9).

original-mother-son.name: Hijo Madre Original
original-mother-son.meaning: The Eternal Son as the original source of the Paradise Sons, who keeps a direct channel with them and approves new creature designs (7:6.7, 21:2.5, 7:5.9).

rejected.reason: An adjective reduces a title to a quality.

second.name: Hijo Madre Original
second.meaning: The Eternal Son as the origin of the Paradise Sons, with whom they keep a direct channel of communication (7:6.7); the 'Eternal and Original Mother Son' whose consent a Creator Son needs for new creature designs (21:2.5).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree and the blind reader and judge match. A title noun 'Madre' keeps the English title, where an adjective would reduce it to a quality.

orlandof.name: Orlandof
orlandof.meaning: A prince and teacher of the blue race who led tribes back to the true God as the 'Supreme Chief'; one of the twenty-four counselors (64:6.23, 45:4.6).

orphic-brotherhood.name: fraternidad órfica
orphic-brotherhood.meaning: The best of the Mediterranean mystery cults, whose moral preachments and promises of salvation appealed to many (98:2.10).

rejected.reason: The fixed root for 'brotherhood' is 'fraternidad'.

orvonon.name: Orvonon
orvonon.meaning: The enlightener of the indigo race who proclaimed 'The God of Gods'; one of the twenty-four counselors (64:6.26, 45:4.10).

orvonton-paradise-satellite.name: Orvonton (satélite del Paraíso)
orvonton-paradise-satellite.meaning: The seventh of the executive spheres of the Infinite Spirit near Paradise, named for and dedicated to the administration of the seventh superuniverse (13:4).

rejected.reason: "luna" names a natural moon; the English says "satellite".

orvonton-superuniverse.name: Orvonton (superuniverso)
orvonton-superuniverse.meaning: The seventh superuniverse, which contains the local universe of Nebadon and Urantia; its capital is Uversa (0:0.5, 15:14).

osiris.name: Osiris
osiris.meaning: The Egyptian god in whose judgment hall the soul of the dead was weighed for admission to bliss or consignment to hell (95:2.9).

oudah.name: oudah
oudah.meaning: The prereligious prayer beliefs of the African Pygmies, beside mana and manitou (91:0.5).

rejected.reason: A spelling change with no source; the papers' spelling stays.

backcheck.reading: Unknown foreign word, perhaps a name or a term in another language.
backcheck.note: A foreign term read as foreign; context defines it.

second.name: oudah
second.meaning: Oudah is the name for the early beliefs and prayer practices of the African Pygmies, named with the mana of the Melanesians and the manitou of the North American Indians as prereligious praying (91:0.5).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; a foreign term stays in the papers' spelling (91:0.5).

outer-space.name: espacio exterior
outer-space.meaning: The space levels beyond the seven superuniverses, where uninhabited universes now mobilize (0:0.6, 12:1, 12:2.4).

rejected.reason: The reader must not bring the astronaut sense "space beyond Earth's atmosphere".
Means "later" more than "farther".

second.name: espacio exterior
second.meaning: The space regions beyond the seven superuniverses, where uninhabited universes mobilize; the four outer space levels of the master universe (0:0.6, 12:1.14, 12:2.1).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree and the judge matches. The context of the space levels beyond the superuniverses (0:0.6, 12:1) removes the astronaut sense.

outerspacers.name: habitantes del espacio exterior
outerspacers.meaning: The future inhabitants of the outer space creations, who can approach Havona through the perfected superuniverses (56:7.9).

rejected.reason: Says they are outside space; outer space is still space.
An adjective, too vague as a noun.
Means beings from beyond Earth, a different idea.

outerspacers.note: The English coins one word; Spanish has no natural one-word form. A reviewer must decide if a coined term is wanted.

backcheck.reading: Beings who live in outer space.

second.name: habitantes del espacio exterior
second.meaning: Outerspacers are the future inhabitants of the outer space universes who may become Havona citizens and help keep the experiential equilibrium of the perfected superuniverses.

adjudicated.reason: The future inhabitants of the outer space creations, 'citizens of the next universe age' (56:7.9, 117:2.7, 55:12.2). 'habitantes' is the plain word for a population and uses 'espacio exterior' from the glossary; 'moradores' is more literary with no gain in meaning.

overcontrol.name: supercontrol
overcontrol.meaning: Control exercised from a higher level over all within a domain, as by the Ultimate over the master universe or by the Unqualified Absolute in infinity (0:1.10, 0:11.8, 118:2.4, 1:2.10).

rejected.reason: Spanish 'sobre-' often means excess, as in sobrecarga; reads as too much control.
Loses the coined single term and the family link.

overcontrol.note: Readers must not take 'super-' as colloquial 'very great'; it names control from a level above, as in Superalma for Oversoul. Family root: control (controladores).

second.name: supercontrol
second.meaning: The control exercised from a higher level over a whole domain: the Ultimate as overcontroller of the master universe, the Unqualified Absolute as a positive overcontrol in infinity, God as cosmic overcontrol of the physical level (0:1.10, 0:11.8, 1:2.10, 10:5.1).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'sobre-' reads as excess in Spanish, and 'super-' gives a coined single term that keeps the family (supercontroladores, supercontrolar).

oversoul-of-creation.name: superalma de la creación
oversoul-of-creation.meaning: The Supreme Being, into whom the personality of a nonsurvivor is absorbed (2:3.4, 117:4.2).

rejected.reason: Loses the root shared with 'Superalma Universal'.

ovid.name: Ovidio
ovid.meaning: A Phoenician teacher who preached the Salem doctrines in Ur, through whom Terah's family learned of Melchizedek (93:5.4).

rejected.reason: The standard Spanish form of the Roman poet; this Ovid is a different person, known only from this book.

ovid.note: Kept in the English spelling because the person exists only in this book; a reviewer can prefer 'Ovidio'.

second.name: Ovid
second.meaning: The Phoenician teacher who proclaimed the Salem doctrines in Ur and through whom Terah's family learned of Melchizedek (93:5.4).

backcheck.note: Form differs from Ovidio; context gives the Phoenician.

adjudicated.reason: Consistency review: Classical authors take their Spanish names (Virgilio, Píndaro).

earlier.reason: Both translators agree. The English spelling keeps this Phoenician teacher of 93:5.4 apart from the Roman poet Ovidio; the doubt is small.

pacific-ocean.name: océano Pacífico
pacific-ocean.meaning: The ocean that formed from the early world ocean and once covered nine tenths of the earth's surface (57:8.20, 57:8.21).

palatine-hill.name: monte Palatino
palatine-hill.meaning: The hill of Rome with the emperor's residence, the temple of Apollo, and the Greek and Latin libraries, where Jesus spent much time (132:0.2).

rejected.reason: Also used, but 'monte Palatino' and 'el Palatino' are the more common Spanish names.

paleozoic.name: Paleozoico
paleozoic.meaning: The marine-life era of 250 million years, ending with the Permian (59:0.4, 59:6.11).

palestine.name: Palestina
palestine.meaning: The land of the eastern Mediterranean where Jesus lived.

palisades-of-the-hudson.name: Palisades del Hudson
palisades-of-the-hudson.meaning: The cliffs along the Hudson River formed by basalt lava forced between Triassic strata (60:1.3).

rejected.reason: A literal translation of a proper geographic name; Spanish texts keep 'Palisades'.

second.name: Palisades del Hudson
second.meaning: The cliffs of the Hudson River formed by the extrusion of basalt lava between Triassic strata (60:1.3).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree and the blind reader understood the cliffs. A literal 'Empalizadas' translates a proper geographic name.

palm-sunday.name: Domingo de Ramos
palm-sunday.meaning: The Sunday on which Jesus left Bethany for his entry into Jerusalem; the papers call it 'that Sunday' and do not use the name Palm Sunday in the passage found (172:3.1).
palm-sunday.note: A full-text search found no use of 'Palm Sunday' in the papers; the entity rests on 172:3.1.

second.name: Domingo de Ramos
second.meaning: The Sunday on which Jesus started from Bethany for Jerusalem, the village where he had chosen to raise Lazarus (172:3.1); the papers describe the day without using the name.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it is the standard Spanish name for the day, and the alias 'aquel domingo' covers the text of 172:3.1, which does not use the name.

palonia.name: Palonia
palonia.meaning: A local system of Nebadon where Lutentia rebelled and where Michael ruled for more than seventeen years as the Savior Sovereign (119:2.5, 119:2.6).

panama-isthmus.name: istmo de Panamá
panama-isthmus.meaning: The isthmus that rose and sank twice in the Cenozoic, joining or separating the Atlantic and Pacific (61:0.2, 61:1.12).

pandora.name: Pandora
pandora.meaning: The Greek figure whom tradition blamed for bringing trouble on man, named as an example of the onetime distrust of woman (84:4.4).

panoptia.name: Panoptia
panoptia.meaning: The only Satania world whose people stayed loyal in the Lucifer rebellion, under Ellanora; Panoptians now care for the Father's world on Jerusem (53:7.1, 53:9.1).

panorama-exhibit-jerusem.name: panorama de exposiciones (Jerusem)
panorama-exhibit-jerusem.meaning: The vast exhibit wall, five thousand miles around the Jerusem circles, that portrays the current status of every peopled world of Satania (46:5.23, 46:5.24).

rejected.reason: "exhibición" can suggest a show or performance in some regions; "exposición" is the plain museum word.
Loses "panorama" as the head noun of the English name.

second.name: panorama de exhibición (Jerusem)
second.meaning: The vast circular exhibit of Jerusem, five thousand standard miles around, which shows the current status of the inhabited worlds of Satania (46:5.23).

adjudicated.reason: 46:5.23: 'the exhibit panorama of Jerusem', which presents the status of each peopled world of Satania. 'Exposición' is the usual Spanish word for an exhibit. Rejected: 'panorama de exhibición' ('exhibición' leans toward a show or performance).

pantaenus.name: Panteno
pantaenus.meaning: A teacher at Alexandria who taught Clement and then followed Nathaniel to proclaim Christ in India (195:3.10).

backcheck.reading: A proper name for an individual, sounding like a Greek-derived name; the meaning is unclear.
misreadings: Could be taken as a misspelling or variant of 'Pantaleón' or of a 'pan-' (all) word.

pantheism.name: panteísmo
pantheism.meaning: The philosophy that denies the personality of God because God has no body; the papers name it, with materialism, as an extreme to avoid (1:5.11, 1:5.12, 103:8.6).

backcheck.reading: The doctrine that God and the universe are the same thing.

paphos.name: Pafos
paphos.meaning: The port in Cyprus where Jesus, Gonod, and Ganid landed before their weeks of rest in the near-by mountains (133:7.2).

backcheck.reading: A place name, a city of ancient Greek or Cypriot character.
misreadings: Could be confused with 'Pafos' on Cyprus, a modern tourist town.

parable-prayers.name: oraciones en parábola
parable-prayers.meaning: Prayers Jesus gave the apostles to illustrate other matters, not to be taught to the multitudes; many came from other planets (144:5.1).

rejected.reason: 'Parabólica' is the geometric curve or a satellite dish.
Turns the prayers into parables.

backcheck.reading: Prayers spoken in the form of parables.
misreadings: Prayers as sentences (oraciones as grammar sentences)
backcheck.note: Prayers in the form of parables is a fair first guess.

second.name: oraciones de parábola
second.meaning: Parable prayers are additional forms of prayer that Jesus mentioned to the apostles in illustration of other matters, told them not to teach to the multitudes, and many of which came from other inhabited planets (144:5.1).

paradise.name: Paraíso
paradise.meaning: The stationary Isle at the geographic center of infinity and the dwelling place of the eternal God (0:0.5, 11:0.1).

rejected.reason: Lowercase reads as the general idea of heaven or the garden; the papers mean a specific place.

second.name: Paraíso
second.meaning: The eternal, stationary Isle at the center of the universe of universes, the abiding place of the Father, Son, and Spirit, a material sphere as well as a spiritual abode (11:0.1, 0:4.12, 0:0.5).

backcheck.reading: The heavenly dwelling of the blessed, a place of perfect bliss.
misreadings: Everyday sense: an idyllic place or garden of delight.
Religious sense: the Garden of Eden or heaven.
Also a common brand or business name.
backcheck.note: Dwelling of God; context completes the Isle.

paradise-arrivals.name: Llegados al Paraíso
paradise-arrivals.meaning: The seventh stage of ascending mortals: those who reach Paradise with residential status, begin the course in divinity and absonity, and are to be mustered into the Mortal Corps of the Finality (30:4.31).

rejected.reason: "llegadas" as a noun is the act of arrival, not the persons who arrive.

second.name: llegados al Paraíso
second.meaning: Ascending mortals who reach Paradise with residential status, before they are mustered into the Corps of the Finality (30:4.31, 30:4.32, 27:2.2).

backcheck.reading: Those who have arrived at Paradise, the arrivals there.
misreadings: Could be read as people who died and reached heaven.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree on the words, and the judge matched. 'Llegados' names the persons, not the act ('Llegadas'), and 'recién' adds a word that the English does not have.

paradise-central-shining.name: Resplandor Central del Paraíso
paradise-central-shining.meaning: The central shining of the spiritual glory of the Universal Father and the eternal Deities at the center of Paradise, with which a servital can have "personal contact" (11:1.3, 13:0.3, 24:7.2); the papers do not say if it is a being or a manifestation.

second.name: Resplandor Central del Paraíso
second.meaning: The central shining of the eternal Deities on Paradise, with which a Havona Servital is granted personal contact before becoming a Graduate Guide (24:7.2, 13:0.3, 11:1.3).

backcheck.reading: A central radiant glow or brilliance of Paradise.
misreadings: Could be read as a natural light or divine glory rather than a person-like being.
backcheck.note: Central glory fits; papers leave it open.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'Resplandor' carries the shining of divine glory without deciding if it is a being or a manifestation, which the papers leave open (24:7.2).

paradise-citizens.name: Ciudadanos del Paraíso
paradise-citizens.meaning: Native resident beings of Paradise, of more than three thousand orders, who are not directly concerned with the ascent of will creatures (30:1, 11:2.11).

rejected.reason: Loses the status sense of "citizens".

forcedChoices: masculine generic "Ciudadanos": Spanish requires a gender; the masculine plural is the neutral generic for a mixed or sexless group.

backcheck.reading: The citizens or inhabitants of Paradise.
misreadings: Could be read as saints or the blessed in heaven.

paradise-companions.name: Compañeros del Paraíso
paradise-companions.meaning: A composite group of angels drawn from several seraphic and supernaphic orders, assigned to keep company with beings, chiefly ascendant mortals, who arrive alone on Paradise (25:8).

rejected.reason: Reads as an escort or attendant role, weaker than companionship.

forcedChoices: masculine generic "Compañeros": Spanish requires a gender; the group is mixed angels, so the generic masculine plural is the neutral form.

misreadings: Could be read as angels or guides in heaven.

paradise-corps-of-the-finality.name: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
aliases: Cuerpos de los Finalitarios del Paraíso
paradise-corps-of-the-finality.meaning: The general name for the seven finality corps mustered on Paradise, of which the Corps of Trinitized Finaliters is one (22:8.6, 26:11.2, 31:10.20).

rejected.form: Cuerpo de la Finalidad del Paraíso
rejected.reason: Closer to the English 'Finality', but the done term 'Corps of the Finality' is 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'; rule 4 requires that form.

Because 'Corps of the Finality' became 'Cuerpo de los Finalitarios', the general 'Paradise Corps of the Finality' and the specific 'Corps of Paradise Finaliters' differ in Spanish only by the article 'los'. 'Cuerpo de la Finalidad' for the done term would keep the two apart.

paradise-corps-of-the-finality.note: Near-collision with corps-of-paradise-finaliters. A reviewer must decide whether to revisit 'Corps of the Finality: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios'.

second.name: Cuerpo de los Finalitarios del Paraíso

misreadings: Everyday sense: finalists in a competition.

paradise-creator-sons.name: Hijos Creadores del Paraíso
paradise-creator-sons.meaning: The Creator Sons (Michaels), who originate on Paradise from the Father and the Son and go out to make and rule local universes (21:0.1, 5:3.6).

paradise-deities.name: Deidades del Paraíso

backcheck.reading: The gods or divinities of Paradise.

paradise-energy.name: energía del Paraíso
paradise-energy.meaning: Energy that takes origin from, or is grasped by, the Isle of Paradise, the source of all cosmic force and the center of absolute gravity (11:8, 105:3.4).

second.name: energía del Paraíso

backcheck.reading: The energy that comes from or belongs to Paradise.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'paradisíaca' means 'delightful' in ordinary Spanish.

paradise-force-organizers.name: organizadores de la fuerza del Paraíso

second.name: organizadores de la fuerza del Paraíso

paradise-gravity.name: gravedad del Paraíso

paradise-havona-system.name: sistema Paraíso-Havona

paradise-havona-trinitized-sons.name: Hijos trinitizados por seres del Paraíso y Havona

second.name: Hijos trinitizados por el Paraíso-Havona

paradise-incarnation-commission.name: comisión de encarnación del Paraíso

paradise-master-spirits.name: Espíritus Maestros del Paraíso

paradise-sons-of-god.name: Hijos de Dios del Paraíso

paradise-source-and-center.name: Fuente y Centro Paraíso

paradise-trinity.name: Trinidad del Paraíso
paradise-trinity.meaning: The eternal union of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, and the Infinite Spirit (10:0.1, 15:0.1).

second.name: Trinidad del Paraíso

paralytic-at-bethsaida.name: paralítico de Betsaida

parsees.name: parsis

patagonians.name: patagones

patmos-isle-of.name: Patmos, isla de

patrae.name: Patras

paul.name: Pablo

pella.name: Pella

pennsylvania.name: Pensilvania

pentecost-bestowal-of-spirit-of-truth.name: Pentecostés (otorgamiento del Espíritu de la Verdad)

perfectors-of-wisdom.name: Perfeccionadores de la Sabiduría
