post-planetary-prince-era.name: era posterior al Príncipe Planetario
post-planetary-prince-era.meaning: The planetary age that follows the arrival of a Planetary Prince on an evolutionary world (no paragraph checked; the sequence of epochs in 47:6.4).

rejected.reason: A prefix before a name of two capitalized words is awkward and unclear in Spanish.

forcedChoices: Spanish cannot join 'post-' to a two-word name as the English does, so the term uses 'posterior al'.

backcheck.reading: The age after a Planetary Prince.
misreadings: Satan as prince of this world
backcheck.note: The age after a Planetary Prince fits.

second.name: era posterior al Príncipe Planetario
second.meaning: The age of a normal world after the Planetary Prince, before the Adamic age (55:0.1, 45:4.4).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; Spanish cannot put 'post-' before a two-word name.

post-teacher-son-era.name: era posterior al Hijo Instructor
post-teacher-son-era.meaning: The planetary age that follows the mission of the Trinity Teacher Sons, before light and life (47:6.4).

rejected.reason: A prefix before a capitalized two-word name is awkward in Spanish.

forcedChoices: Spanish cannot join 'post-' to a two-word name; 'posterior al' is used, and the singular follows the English 'Teacher Son'.

backcheck.reading: The age after a Son who is a teacher.
backcheck.note: The age after a teacher Son fits.

second.name: era posterior al Hijo Instructor
second.meaning: The age of a world after the missions of the Trinity Teacher Sons, the stage before the age of light and life (47:6.4, 52:0.7).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree, and it follows 'Teacher Sons: Hijos Instructores'.

potential.name: Potencial
potential.meaning: Reality that carries undisclosed capacity for growth; capitalized, the triodity of the Deity, Unqualified, and Universal Absolutes (0:4.7, 115:3.8, 115:3.16).

rejected.reason: A possibility is not a capacity for growth, and it breaks the family 'potencialidad'.

second.name: lo Potencial
second.meaning: Reality that carries undisclosed capacity for growth, in contrast with the Actual that exists in fullness of expression; mortal man is largely an unrealized spiritual potentiality (0:4.7, 0:4.4).

backcheck.reading: Potential, a capacity that could be realized.
misreadings: Everyday sense: electric potential or possibility.

potentials.name: potenciales
potentials.meaning: Realities not yet actual that exist in the Absolutes and become actual through the transcendental agencies and the Trinity; in evolving universes the potential is supreme over the actual.

rejected.reason: Longer, and the done term 'Potencial' fixes the root.
Can mean powers or nations, or a mathematical power.

power.name: poder
power.meaning: Ordinarily the electronic level of material, linear-gravity-responsive matter; the papers also use it for sovereignty (0:6.2, 0:6.7).

rejected.reason: Covers only the physical sense and loses sovereignty; 'Poder' is used in 'Directores del Poder del Universo'.

second.name: poder
second.meaning: Ordinarily the electronic level of matter that responds to linear gravity in the grand universe; also used for sovereignty (0:6.2, 0:6.7).

misreadings: Everyday sense: political power, electric power or the verb 'can'.
backcheck.note: Same range of senses as the English.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'poder' keeps both senses of 0:6.2 and 0:6.7 and matches 'Directores del Poder del Universo'.

power-centers.name: centros del poder
power-centers.meaning: Beings who regulate power in the universes; with the physical controllers they direct physical evolution after the force organizers (41:1.1, 29:2.18).

misreadings: Everyday sense: power plants or political centers.

power-supervisors.name: supervisores del poder
power-supervisors.meaning: The Morontia Power Supervisors, who unite material and spiritual energies into morontia forms (29:0.11, 48:1.5).
power-supervisors.note: The papers use the phrase only as part of 'Morontia Power Supervisors' (29:0.11).

second.name: supervisores del poder
second.meaning: Short form for the Morontia Power Supervisors, 'the supervisors of morontia power' with whom ascenders work on the mansion worlds (29:0.11, 46:5.26).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. The form is the short form of the Morontia Power Supervisors (29:0.11).

power-transformers.name: transformadores del poder
power-transformers.meaning: Physical controllers who modify energies, for example to light Jerusem and at the wine of Cana (46:1.4, 137:4.12).

rejected.reason: That is the form of 'energy transformers'.

powers-of-paradise.name: Poderes del Paraíso
powers-of-paradise.meaning: The divine presences on Paradise into whose presence ascending angels and mortals come at last, in context the Paradise Deities (27:7.6).

rejected.reason: "Potestades" names a rank of angels in Christian tradition, a sense the authors do not intend.
"fuerza" is a technical term for physical force in the papers.

second.name: Poderes del Paraíso
second.meaning: The high beings of Paradise, apparently the Paradise Deities, whose presence angels and mortals of time attain at the end of the ascent (27:7.6, 0:4.13).

misreadings: Religious sense: the angelic order of Powers.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'Potestades' names a Christian angelic rank, and 'Fuerzas' collides with the physical term 'fuerza'.

praetorium.name: pretorio
praetorium.meaning: The addition to the fortress of Antonia where Pilate stayed in Jerusalem and before which he tried Jesus (185:0.2, 185:0.3).

backcheck.reading: The praetorium, a Roman official residence or court.
misreadings: Religious sense: where Pilate judged Jesus.

prajapati.name: Prajapati
prajapati.meaning: A name for the deity-father principle of the Vedic religion, sometimes called Brahma (94:1.4).

backcheck.reading: Prajapati, a Hindu deity, lord of creatures.

prayer.name: oración
prayer.meaning: The sincere communication of the creature with the spirit Father, a process of exchanging the human will for the divine will (144:4.9, 91:8).

rejected.reason: Suggests a recited formula; the papers set true prayer apart from repetition and ritual.
Correct but literary; 'oración' is the plain common word and matches 'Oración del Señor' in the glossary.
Only petition; the papers give prayer a wider sense than asking.

prayer-of-identification.name: oración de identificación
prayer-of-identification.meaning: The prayer of a Master Spirit before the Infinite Spirit when a Creator Son is commissioned, at which the future Creative Spirit first appears as distinct (17:6.5).

rejected.reason: 'Oración' is the plain word and is used across the glossary.

backcheck.reading: A prayer in which one identifies with God or another.
backcheck.note: As opaque as the English; context gives the Master Spirit scene.

pre-sumerians.name: presumerios
pre-sumerians.meaning: Nodites near the mouth of the Tigris and Euphrates who kept the Dalamatian culture and later blended with the Adamites (78:1.4, 77:4.6).

rejected.reason: RAE writes the prefix joined.

backcheck.reading: Presumerians, a people before the Sumerians.

prelife-era.name: era anterior a la vida
prelife-era.meaning: The cataclysmic age before life appeared on Urantia, the Archeozoic (59:0.3).

rejected.reason: 'Previda' is not a word in Spanish.

second.name: era previa a la vida
second.meaning: The prelife era is the first 450 million years of the planet, from when it reached its present size until life began; it is the Archeozoic (59:0.2).

adjudicated.reason: 59:0.2-3: the Archeozoic, before life began on the planet. 'anterior' is the plainer word of time; both candidates carry the meaning.

prepersonal-entities.name: entidades prepersonales
prepersonal-entities.meaning: Entities that are not persons, as the Adjusters and the unrevealed entities of the Father on Divinington (107:3.1).

rejected.reason: 'Entity' is not 'being'; the English keeps them apart.

backcheck.reading: Entities that are not yet persons or are below personal.

presence-circuits.name: circuitos de presencia
presence-circuits.meaning: The four absolute circuits of Paradise gravity (personality, spiritual, mind, and material) that pervade the superuniverses and are independent of time and space (12:3.6, 15:9.1).

rejected.reason: 'Presencial' reads as 'in person', as for a meeting.

presence-embellishers.name: embellecedores de la presencia
presence-embellishers.meaning: Artisans who arrange morontia and spirit beings in composite ensembles, like living notes, odors, and sights, to dramatize relationship (44:6.7).

rejected.reason: Suggests self-adornment, which 44:6.7 says they do not do.

presence-embellishers.note: 'presencia' must be read as the presence of beings in an ensemble, not personal appearance.

second.name: embellecedores de la presencia
second.meaning: Designers and embellishers (celestial artisans) who arrange supermaterial beings as living notes, odors, and sights, and so dramatize the significance of relationship through positional values (44:6.7).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'personales' would suggest self-adornment, which 44:6.7 excludes.

priest-s-title.name: título sacerdotal de propiedad
priest-s-title.meaning: The right to land that priests consecrated and placed under magic taboos, marked with stones bearing the priest's initials (69:9.13).

rejected.reason: Reads as the rank of a priest.
Reads as sacred writing or scripture.

priest-s-title.note: 'Título sacerdotal' can also read as a priestly rank; the context of property must carry the sense of a title deed.

misreadings: A title of nobility for clergy
backcheck.note: Read as a priestly rank, not a right to land.

second.name: título del sacerdote
second.meaning: A priest's title is the early form of land ownership: the priests consecrated a piece of land, and its owner was said to hold a priest's title, protected by magic taboos and by stone markers with the priest's initials (69:9.13).

adjudicated.reason: 69:9.13: a right to land that priests consecrated and marked with stones. 'título sacerdotal' alone reads as a priestly rank; 'de propiedad' shows that it is a title to land.

primary-associators.name: asociadores primarios
primary-associators.meaning: Master Physical Controllers who store and conserve energy and act as living catalysts that convert space energies into physical states (29:4.32).

rejected.reason: "asociado" is reserved for "associate".

primary-associators.note: "asociador" is a rare word in Spanish but it reads as a term, as the English does.

second.name: asociadores primarios
second.meaning: Master Physical Controllers that store energy during plus manifestations and convert the energies of space into physical states, acting by their presence like living catalysts (29:4.32).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'asociado' is fixed for 'associate', and the rare 'asociador' reads as a term, as the English does.

primary-eruption.name: erupción primaria
primary-eruption.meaning: The tremendous spiritual flash on Paradise at the personalization of a local universe Mother Spirit (34:1.1, 17:6.7).

rejected.reason: 'Erupción' keeps the English word, which the papers put in quotes.

backcheck.note: A first eruption is a fair first guess for the flash.

primary-eventuated-master-force-organize.name: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza Eventuados Primarios
primary-eventuated-master-force-organize.meaning: The first order of Master Force Organizers, whose space presence makes passive force active (29:5.2, 42:2.8).

rejected.reason: 'eventual' means possible or temporary
loses the special sense of 'eventuate' (absonite emergence)

second.name: Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza Eventuados Primarios
second.meaning: The first division of the Master Force Organizers, whose space presence turns passive and potential force into active primordial force (29:0.2, 42:2.8).

misreadings: Everyday sense: engineers organizing a military force.

adjudicated.reason: 29:5.2 and 42:2.8: the first division of the Master Force Organizers. The order follows 'Organizadores Maestros de la Fuerza Trascendentales Asociados' (Associate Transcendental). Rejected: 'Primarios Eventuados' (breaks that fixed pattern).

primates.name: Primates
primates.meaning: The particular species, sprung from the mid-mammals, that were the direct animal ancestors of the human race and soon died out (62:4.2, 62:4.7).

rejected.reason: In Spanish it is the whole zoological order (monkeys, apes, humans); the papers name one species, so the capital stays.

primates.note: A reader can take "Primates" as the zoological order; only the capital marks the difference.

second.name: Primates
second.meaning: The species of animals that came from the mid-mammals as the third vital mutation and were the direct and immediate animal ancestors of the human family (62:4.2, 62:4.7, 61:6.1).

backcheck.reading: Primates, the order of mammals including apes and humans.
misreadings: Religious sense: primate as a church dignitary.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. The capital marks the one species of 62:4 and keeps it apart from the zoological order.

primitive-mortals.name: mortales primitivos
primitive-mortals.meaning: Mortals in the early stages of evolution on a world, before advanced civilization (e.g. 39:5.7 'primitive men').

rejected.reason: 'Primigenio' means 'original, first of all', which changes the idea from 'early stage' to 'origin'.

second.name: mortales primitivos
second.meaning: Early evolutionary humans in the first age of a world, cave dwellers, often too immature for Adjuster fusion (52:1.5, 49:6.6, 52:1.8).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree. 'primigenios' changes the idea from an early stage to an origin.

primordial-force.name: fuerza primordial
primordial-force.meaning: Pure energy, the primal force that is preresponsive to gravity and personally controlled by the Universal Father (56:1.3).

rejected.reason: Equal in meaning but less common.

prince-of-darkness.name: príncipe de las tinieblas
prince-of-darkness.meaning: A title of Caligastia, the fallen Planetary Prince of Urantia (179:2.3, 176:2.3).

rejected.reason: Plain, but 'tinieblas' is the usual Spanish for 'darkness' in this moral sense.

prince-of-devils.name: príncipe de los demonios
prince-of-devils.meaning: A charge against Jesus: that he did his works by the power of the prince of devils (154:4.4, 162:7.4).

rejected.reason: 'diablo' also is an exclamation and a joking word.

prince-of-peace.name: Príncipe de Paz
prince-of-peace.meaning: A title of the bestowal Son, who on normal worlds brings an age of peace; the papers apply it to Jesus and deny it to the Planetary Prince (52:6.1, 52:2.5, 68:3.5).

rejected.reason: Also used in Spanish, but the English has no article; both are natural.

prince-of-salem.name: Príncipe de Salem
prince-of-salem.meaning: The local title of Machiventa Melchizedek, who presided over a small colony of truth seekers at Salem in Abraham's time (35:4.5).

misreadings: Religious sense: Melchizedek, king of Salem.

prince-of-this-world.name: Príncipe de este mundo
prince-of-this-world.meaning: Caligastia, the fallen Planetary Prince, as Jesus named him (53:8.5, 136:3.1, 174:5.12).

misreadings: Religious sense: Satan in John's Gospel.

prince-s-corporeal-staff.name: personal corpóreo del Príncipe
prince-s-corporeal-staff.meaning: The material helpers of a Planetary Prince, removed at the next adjudication (50:3.4).

rejected.reason: 'cuerpo' translates 'Corps'; the fixed root is 'personal'.

backcheck.reading: The embodied staff of the Prince.

priscilla.name: Priscila
priscilla.meaning: A Jewish refugee from Rome, Aquila's wife and a tentmaker, with whom Paul lived and worked in Corinth (133:3.12).

misreadings: Religious sense: Priscilla, companion of Paul.

prison-worlds.name: mundos prisión
prison-worlds.meaning: The seven satellites around the Father's world of Jerusem used as detention spheres for Lucifer and his followers (45:1.10, 45:1.11).

rejected.reason: Suggests a penal system for correction, which the text does not state.

probationary-nursery.name: guardería probatoria
probationary-nursery.meaning: The system finaliter world where Adjuster-indwelt children who die before they choose the Paradise career are raised; parents can serve there (49:6.11, 45:6.8).

rejected.reason: 'Probación' also means a religious novitiate.
'Vivero' is a plant nursery or fish farm.
Reads as a trial or test daycare.

probationary-nursery.note: 'Probatorio' in common Spanish leans to legal proof ('periodo probatorio'). A reviewer can prefer a form that says 'a period before the choice'.

second.name: guardería probatoria
second.meaning: The place on the system finaliter world where Adjuster-indwelt children who died before choosing the Paradise career are raised, their survival being dependent on a later choice (49:6.11, 45:6.8).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators and the judge agree. 'Guardería' gives the care of children; 'probatoria' marks the period before the choice (49:6.11) better than the rejected forms, which bring a novitiate or a test daycare.

proclamation-of-equality.name: Proclamación de Igualdad
proclamation-of-equality.meaning: Michael of Nebadon's final proclamation of the Creative Mother Spirit's equality with him, the pattern for family and voluntary marriage (33:3.6).

rejected.reason: Adds an article that the English title does not have.

misreadings: Everyday sense: Emancipation Proclamation, a civil rights declaration.

prodigal-son.name: hijo pródigo
prodigal-son.meaning: The son in Jesus' parable who wastes his inheritance and is received back by his father (169:1).

backcheck.reading: The prodigal son, a child who leaves home, wastes all, and returns.

progress-angels.name: ángeles del progreso
progress-angels.meaning: Master seraphim of planetary supervision who start the progress of the successive social ages (114:6.6).

progress-helpers.name: asistentes del progreso
progress-helpers.meaning: The more spiritual midwayers, distributed as assistants to seraphim who work in special groups on the planet (77:8.9).

rejected.reason: 'helper' is 'asistente' in done terms (pilgrim helpers, planetary helper seraphim); 'ayudante' is 'adjutant'.

prometheus.name: Prometeo
prometheus.meaning: The legendary figure said to have stolen fire from heaven, a legend that replaced the story of Andon and the flint (81:2.9).

backcheck.reading: Prometheus, the Greek titan who gave fire to humans.

promised-land.name: Tierra Prometida
promised-land.meaning: The land 'that flowed with milk and honey' that the Arabian Semites tried to enter (96:2.2).

misreadings: Religious sense: Canaan, promised to the Hebrews.

promoters-of-oratory.name: promotores de la oratoria
promoters-of-oratory.meaning: Thought recorders who preserve thought for reproduction by speech (44:4.7).

prophetic-artists.name: artistas proféticos
prophetic-artists.meaning: Heavenly reproducers who project the meanings of history into the future (44:2.7).
prophetic-artists.note: 'proféticos' can bring a religious sense of foretelling by inspiration; the text means projecting historical meanings forward.

second.name: artistas proféticos
second.meaning: Heavenly reproducers (celestial artisans) who project the meanings of history into the future (44:2.7).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators and the judge agree, and the term is used in one paragraph (44:2.7), where the context shows the projection of history. No candidate is clearly better.

proterozoic.name: Proterozoico
proterozoic.meaning: The life-dawn era of geologic history, between the prelife age and the era of developed marine life (59:0.3, 58:7.1).

protestant-reformation.name: Reforma protestante
aliases: ruptura de la unidad del cristianismo
protestant-reformation.meaning: The fifteenth-century disruption of the unity of Christianity in the Occident, when institutional Christianity became too rigid to grow and stay united (92:5.15).
protestant-reformation.note: The papers do not use the name; 92:5.15 says 'the disruption of the unity of Christianity'. In a translation of that sentence, translate the description, not the name.

second.name: Reforma protestante
second.meaning: The disruption of the unity of Christianity in the Occident in the fifteenth century, when institutionalized Christianity had become too inelastic for further growth within unity (92:5.15); the papers do not use the words 'Protestant Reformation'.

adjudicated.reason: Standard Spanish name; both translators and the judge agree. The note stays: translate the description in 92:5.15, not the name.

protozoa.name: Protozoos
protozoa.meaning: The primitive single-celled animal organisms, such as the ameba, that survive from the first steps of life differentiation (58:7.2, 65:2.4).

rejected.reason: Correct but less common than 'protozoos' in neutral Spanish.

proverbs.name: Proverbios
proverbs.meaning: The Hebrew Book of Proverbs of the Old Testament, parts of which the papers say are taken almost verbatim from Amenemope's Book of Wisdom (95:4.5, 95:4.3).

rejected.reason: Ordinary word for sayings; loses the reference to the biblical book.

backcheck.reading: Proverbs, sayings or the biblical book.

providence.name: providencia
providence.meaning: The watchcare of God and the co-ordination of universe events for the good of creatures, partly the emergence of the Supreme; it does not mean that God decides all things in advance (118:10).

backcheck.reading: Divine providence, God's care and guidance of events.

psalms.name: Salmos
psalms.meaning: The Book of Psalms, a collection of hymns that records varying concepts of God from Amenemope to Isaiah; Jesus recited psalms on the cross (96:7.3, 187:5.2).

backcheck.reading: Psalms, the biblical book of songs.

psychic-circles.name: círculos psíquicos
psychic-circles.meaning: The seven levels of mortal personality growth, from the seventh to the first, that measure the attainment of mind and spirit (110:6).

rejected.reason: Loses the coined word 'psychic'.
Spanish 'psíquico' in popular use means paranormal; the papers mean 'of the mind and soul'.

backcheck.reading: Circles or levels of the psyche or mind.

second.name: círculos psíquicos
second.meaning: The psychic circles are seven levels of cosmic growth that a mortal passes, from the seventh up to the first, as personality realizes itself and approaches Adjuster fusion (110:6.1, 110:6.16).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree, and it matches 'siete círculos psíquicos' in the glossary.

psychic-organization.name: organización psíquica
psychic-organization.meaning: The basic orders of mental organization, twenty-four in man, which match the twenty-four pattern units of the life-carrying bundle (36:2.16).

rejected.reason: Loses 'psychic', which the papers use in a set sense.

psychic-organization.note: The reader must not bring the paranormal sense of 'psíquico'.

backcheck.reading: The organization of the psyche or mind.
backcheck.note: The organization of the mind fits.

second.name: organización psíquica
second.meaning: Psychic organization is the basic pattern of mind in living beings; there are twenty-four basic orders that follow the twenty-four pattern units of the life-carrying material (36:2.16).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree, and it keeps 'psíquico' as in 'círculos psíquicos'.

ptolemais.name: Tolemaida
ptolemais.meaning: A coastal city of Palestine on Jesus' routes (128:3.2, 156:6.2).

ptolemies.name: Ptolomeos
ptolemies.meaning: The Greek dynasty of Egypt to the south of the Jews (121:2.8).

rejected.reason: Correct but less known.

backcheck.reading: The Ptolemies, the Hellenistic dynasty of Egypt.

adjudicated.reason: Follows the form 'Ptolomeo' of the single king; 'Lágidas' is correct but less known.

ptolemy.name: Ptolomeo
ptolemy.meaning: The Greek king of Egypt who had the spurious creation document translated into Greek by seventy scholars for his library at Alexandria (74:8.12).

rejected.reason: Also correct Spanish; 'Ptolomeo' is the more common form.

second.name: Ptolomeo
second.meaning: The Greek king of Egypt who had the spurious Mosaic creation document translated into Greek by seventy scholars for the library at Alexandria (74:8.12).

backcheck.reading: Ptolemy, the astronomer or a king of Egypt.
misreadings: Everyday sense: Ptolemy the astronomer of the earth-centered system.
backcheck.note: King of Egypt is a first guess; context completes.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it is the more common Spanish spelling, and 74:8.12 makes the king of Egypt clear.

public-builders.name: constructores públicos
public-builders.meaning: The seventh group of divine builders among the celestial artisans, who plan and construct the places of assembly other than those of worship (44:3.8).

rejected.reason: Adds a sense of civil engineering that the English does not have.

public-builders.note: 'constructores públicos' can read as builders employed by a government. The English has the same weakness.

second.name: constructores de lugares públicos
second.meaning: The divine builders who plan and construct the places of assembly other than those of worship (44:3.8).

misreadings: Everyday sense: construction workers for public works.

adjudicated.reason: 44:3.8 names them 'the public builders' and then explains them. The plain form follows the English; 'de lugares públicos' explains instead of naming.

puget-sound.name: estrecho de Puget
puget-sound.meaning: The inlet of the Pacific through which icebergs slipped out in the ice age (61:5.8).

rejected.reason: 'sonda' is a probe; a false translation of 'sound'.

second.name: estrecho de Puget
second.meaning: The inlet on the Pacific coast of North America through which icebergs slid into the Pacific during the early ice age (61:5.8).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it is the usual Spanish name and avoids the false 'sonda'.

puissant-energy.name: energía pujante
puissant-energy.meaning: The first stage of energy that the primary force organizers make from primordial force: powerful-directional and not at first responsive to Paradise gravity (29:5.5, 42:2.11).

rejected.reason: 'Poder' translates 'power', a separate technical term (universe power).
Can be confused with 'potencia' and 'potencial'.

puissant-energy.note: English 'puissant' is a rare, old word; 'pujante' (vigorous) keeps it rare and strong, but a reviewer must agree.

backcheck.reading: A strong, pushing, or thriving energy.

second.name: energía pujante
second.meaning: Puissant energy is the first emergent phase of energy, made from primordial force by the Primary Master Force Organizers; it is strong and directional and later yields to Paradise gravity (42:2.13).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; 'pujante' keeps a rare, strong word and avoids 'poder' (power) and 'potencia'.

punjab.name: Punyab
punjab.meaning: The region of northwestern India that received a continuous infiltration of Andite and Aryan blood (79:1.1, 79:4.3).

rejected.reason: Also accepted, but less common.
English spelling; Spanish usage adapts 'j' to 'y'.

second.name: Punjab
second.meaning: The region of northern India that the Andites entered from the Turkestan highlands and that kept receiving Aryan blood down to the first century before Christ (79:1.1, 79:4.3).

backcheck.reading: Punjab, the region of India and Pakistan.

adjudicated.reason: 79:1.1 and 79:4.3: the region of northern India. 'Punyab' is the Spanish spelling that gives the right sound. Rejected: 'Punjab' (Spanish 'j' gives the wrong sound).

pure-energy.name: energía pura
pure-energy.meaning: Primordial force, preresponsive to gravity, of which God is the source as he is of pure spirit (56:1.3, 107:6.4).

rejected.reason: Longer, with no gain.

misreadings: Spiritual pure energy in New Age

pure-in-heart.name: puros de corazón
pure-in-heart.meaning: In the fourth beatitude, those whose spiritual purity lacks suspicion and revenge and who have the faith a parent has in a child, so they love with a fatherly love (140:3.6, 140:5.12).

rejected.reason: Good Spanish too, but 140:5.12 builds on the noun 'purity' (pureza); 'puros' keeps that link visible.
140:5.12 says Jesus did not mean sex attitudes only; 'casto' narrows it to that.

backcheck.reading: The pure in heart, from the Beatitudes.

purim.name: Purim
purim.meaning: The spring feast of Esther and Israel's deliverance through her (123:3.5).

pygmies.name: pigmeos
pygmies.meaning: The Pygmies of Africa, cited as surviving backward, nonsocial peoples without a marriage institution (68:1.6, 82:2.2).

pyrenees.name: Pirineos
pyrenees.meaning: The mountain range whose highlands stood above water as islands when most of Europe was submerged (61:1.12).

backcheck.reading: The Pyrenees, mountains between Spain and France.

qualified-absolute.name: Absoluto Condicionado
qualified-absolute.meaning: The Deity Absolute, the absolute potential segregated by the Father's choice, in contrast to the Unqualified Absolute (0:11.6, 0:10.1).

rejected.reason: 'Cualificado' means 'skilled, trained'.

second.name: Absoluto Condicionado

backcheck.note: Conditioned is a fair equivalent of qualified.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators and the judge agree; 'condicionado' carries 'qualified' as limited, while 'cualificado' and 'calificado' mean skilled. It pairs with 'Absoluto Incondicionado'.

qualified-vicegerents-of-the-ultimate.name: Vicegerentes Condicionados del Último
qualified-vicegerents-of-the-ultimate.meaning: Beings who represent the Ultimate, influential in the superuniverse governments and represented by Reflective Image Aids, whose present whereabouts and function the papers do not reveal (15:10.21, 106:4.3, 117:7.4).

rejected.reason: 'Calificado' means skilled or graded; 'Qualified' is 'Condicionado' in 'Absoluto Condicionado', so it stays 'Condicionado'.

second.name: Vicegerentes Condicionados del Último
second.meaning: Beings who hold delegated authority of the Ultimate, influential in the superuniverse governments but not fully active, represented by the Reflective Image Aids; their whereabouts and function are not revealed (15:10.21, 106:4.3, 117:7.4).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; 'Condicionados' keeps the same rendering of 'Qualified' as in 'Absoluto Condicionado', and 'Vicegerentes' keeps the delegated authority.

quarantine.name: cuarentena
quarantine.meaning: The isolation of a rebel world or system from the normal circuits and communication, as Satania under a Norlatiadek quarantine (46:8.2, 53:8).

rejected.reason: Translates 'isolation', a separate English word.

misreadings: A medical isolation such as during an epidemic

quebec.name: Quebec
quebec.meaning: The region of Canada with lava flows from the coral period (59:3.2).

backcheck.reading: Quebec, the Canadian province or city.

queensland.name: Queensland
queensland.meaning: The Australian region where the first child is still often killed and eaten (89:5.4).

quickeners-of-morality.name: vivificadores de la moralidad
quickeners-of-morality.meaning: Administrator seraphim who quicken the appreciation of cosmic morality, the interactions of liberty and loyalty, and portray mortal life as an unbroken chain (39:4.10, 39:4.13).

rejected.reason: 'quicken' here is to enliven, not to make faster.

second.name: avivadores de la moralidad
second.meaning: Seraphic teachers who quicken, on the mansion worlds and system headquarters, the ascender's appreciation of cosmic morality, of liberty and loyalty (39:4.10, 39:4.13).

adjudicated.reason: 39:4.10: they quicken, that is make alive and keen, the appreciation of cosmic morality. 'Vivificar' carries that sense and reads as a term; 'avivar' suggests stirring a fire or a crowd.

race-commissioners.name: comisionados de las razas
race-commissioners.meaning: High Commissioners in their first planetary service, who interpret and speak for the needs of the human races (37:5.5, 48:6.22).

rejected.reason: "racial" in Spanish can suggest racial policy or discrimination.

second.name: comisionados raciales
second.meaning: High Commissioners at the start of their service, who speak for a mortal race on its planet and seek mercy, justice, and fair treatment for it (37:5.5, 37:5.6, 48:6.22).

adjudicated.reason: 37:5.5 and 37:5.6: they speak for the mortal races of a planet. Rejected: 'comisionados raciales' ('racial' reads as a modern political or race-relations office).

races.name: razas
races.meaning: The human races of Urantia: the Andonites, the six Sangik races, and later blends with Nodites and Adamites (63:4.1, 64:6.1, 78:4.3).

second.name: razas
second.meaning: The human stocks of an evolutionary world, among them the six evolutionary races of color that on Urantia appeared at once in one family (64:6.1).

rachel-old-testament.name: Raquel (Antiguo Testamento)
rachel-old-testament.meaning: Jacob's wife, who hid sacred stones in her tent (85:1.1).

backcheck.reading: Rachel of the Old Testament, wife of Jacob.

rachel-sister-in-law-of-jude.name: Raquel (cuñada de Judas, hermano de Jesús)
rachel-sister-in-law-of-jude.meaning: The sister-in-law of Jude, Jesus' brother, one of the ten women whom Jesus set apart for the ministry of the kingdom (150:1.1, 154:6.1).

backcheck.reading: A woman named Rachel, sister-in-law of Judas, brother of Jesus.
misreadings: Could be confused with the biblical Rachel.

racial-interpreters.name: intérpretes raciales
racial-interpreters.meaning: A group of seraphic transition ministers who help the race commissioners harmonize the differing viewpoints of the races on the inhabited worlds and the mansion worlds; 'sociologists and ethnic advisers of the first heaven' (48:6.22, 39:6.3).

rejected.reason: Suggests translation of languages; these beings interpret viewpoints, not words.
Acceptable, but longer and reads less as a term.

misreadings: Everyday sense: translators between races or languages.

ragaba.name: Ragaba
ragaba.meaning: A town of Perea in the final mission, where the Pharisee Nathaniel gave a Sabbath breakfast for Jesus (165:0.1, 166:1.1).

backcheck.reading: A place name, Ragaba, of unclear meaning.

ramah.name: Ramá
ramah.meaning: A Galilean town where the apostles worked and where Jesus talked with an aged Greek philosopher (146:3.1, 138:9.3, 156:6.2).

misreadings: Could be read as a branch (rama).

ramath.name: Ramat
ramath.meaning: One of the towns of Perea where the seventy worked in the Perean mission (165:0.1).

rejected.reason: That is the form of Ramah, a different town in the papers (146:0.1).

second.name: Ramat
second.meaning: One of the cities and towns of Perea worked by the seventy messengers, Jesus, and the twelve during the Perean mission (165:0.1).

backcheck.reading: A place name, Ramat, Hebrew for height.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it keeps this town apart from Ramah (Ramá).

ramman.name: Ramman
ramman.meaning: A Babylonian god of the air to whom Rimmon was once dedicated (146:1.1).

backcheck.reading: Ramman, a name of unknown origin; perhaps a Semitic deity.

rantowoc.name: Rantowoc
rantowoc.meaning: A wise man of the red race, the first mortal on Urantia to have a personal guardian of destiny (113:2.2).

backcheck.reading: Rantowoc, an unfamiliar name, perhaps Native American.

rantulia.name: Rantulia
rantulia.meaning: A local system of Norlatiadek next to Satania, through which the loyal intelligence corps sent calls for help to Edentia in the Lucifer rebellion (41:2.1, 53:6.5).

rapture.name: técnica de desmaterialización
rapture.meaning: In the packet, the dematerialization technique for removing a whole population to a new world when a physical catastrophe dooms its planet (51:2.3).

rejected.reason: Already the done term for 'Son seizure'.
In common Spanish means kidnapping.

rapture.note: A search finds no use of the word 'rapture' in the papers; the paragraph speaks only of a 'dematerialization technique'. The Christian sense of 'rapture' is not in the text. A human must decide if this term stays in the glossary.

backcheck.reading: A sudden fit of emotion, an outburst.
misreadings: The Rapture of believers in evangelical teaching
backcheck.note: Read as a fit of emotion, not the removal of a population.

second.name: técnica de desmaterialización
second.meaning: The only match in the papers for this entry is the dematerialization technique that the Melchizedeks and Life Carriers install to carry a whole endangered population by seraphic transport to a new world (51:2.3); the word 'rapture' itself is not in the papers.

adjudicated.reason: The word 'rapture' is not in the papers; the only match is the dematerialization technique of 51:2.3. 'arrebato' brings in the evangelical Rapture, a doctrine the authors do not teach. Low confidence in the meaning of the entry.

ratta.name: Ratta
ratta.meaning: Adamson's Nodite wife; with him she had sixty-seven children, among them the origin of the secondary midwayers (77:5.6).

raw-eaters.name: comecrudos
raw-eaters.meaning: A term of derision, after fire led to cooking, for those who still ate uncooked food (69:6.7).

rejected.reason: 'Comedores' also means dining rooms.
The modern name of a raw-food diet, with no derision.

backcheck.note: People who eat raw food fits.

second.name: comedores de crudo
second.meaning: 'Raw eaters' became a term of derision after fire led to cooking, for those who still ate uncooked food (69:6.7).

adjudicated.reason: 69:6.7: a term of derision for those who still ate uncooked food. A compound like 'comecrudos' is the natural Spanish form for a mocking name.

reality.name: realidad
reality.meaning: All that exists on every universe level, originating in the infinite volition of the Universal Father and actualizing differentially in primal phases on many levels (0:4.1, 0:6.11).

rejected.reason: False friend: means the present time; the papers keep 'actual' and 'reality' apart.

second.name: realidad
second.meaning: That which exists, originating in the infinite volition of the Father and actualizing on diverse universe levels, deified, undeified, and interassociated (0:4.1, 0:4.2, 0:4.4).

realization-of-identity-transition.name: transición de realización de la identidad
realization-of-identity-transition.meaning: The state into which an Adjuster passes after it registers at Divinington, until it is summoned on the third period to the mansion world with the surviving soul (112:4.13).

rejected.form: transición de toma de conciencia de la identidad
rejected.reason: Closes 'realization' to 'becoming aware', which the English does not decide.

forcedChoices: 'Realization' can mean making real or becoming aware; 'realización' keeps 'making real' only, the reading that the transit to a new personality form supports best.

backcheck.reading: A passage or transit in which one's identity is realized.
backcheck.note: A passage where identity is realized is a fair first guess.

second.name: transición de la toma de conciencia de la identidad
second.meaning: The 'realization of identity transition' is the state into which a surviving mortal's Adjuster passes after it registers at Divinington and is recognized by the chief Personalized Monitor, until it is called to the mansion world to the resurrected personality (112:4.13).

adjudicated.reason: 112:4.13 puts the phrase in quotes as a coined name. English 'realization' can mean to make real or to become aware; Spanish forces a choice, and 'realización' keeps the sense of making real, which the context of the Adjuster's state supports. 'toma de conciencia' closes the other reading.

rebecca-daughter-of-ezra.name: Rebeca (hija de Esdras)
rebecca-daughter-of-ezra.meaning: The eldest daughter of Ezra, a merchant of Nazareth, who fell in love with Jesus (127:5.1).

misreadings: Could be confused with biblical Rebekah.

rebecca-daughter-of-joseph-of-arimathea.name: Rebeca (hija de José de Arimatea)
rebecca-daughter-of-joseph-of-arimathea.meaning: The daughter of Joseph of Arimathea, added by Jesus to the women's corps; she heard the women's report of the resurrection (150:1.1, 190:1.2).

rejected.reason: The terms already done use the standard Spanish 'Rebeca' (Rebecca, daughter of Ezra).

backcheck.reading: Rebecca, daughter of Joseph of Arimathea.

rebellion-spiritual.name: rebelión (espiritual)
rebellion-spiritual.meaning: Deliberate revolt of personal beings against the rule of the Father and the universe order, as in the Lucifer rebellion, which isolates the worlds that join it (53:0, 53:1.4, 46:8.2).

rejected.reason: The papers use 'insurrection' as a separate word (53:1.4); keep 'rebelión' for 'rebellion' as in 'rebelión de Lucifer'.
Military sense.

backcheck.reading: A spiritual rebellion against divine authority.
backcheck.note: A revolt against divine authority fits.

recents-of-days.name: Recientes de Días
recents-of-days.meaning: The youngest supreme Trinity directors of the superuniverses, 21,000 in number, who rule the minor sectors in groups of three, co-ordinate in nature with the Perfections of Days but subordinate in authority (18:5.1, 18:5.4, 15:13.6).

rejected.reason: The done list has 'Ancianos de Días' and 'Uniones de Días' without the article.

backcheck.reading: Recent of Days, a class of beings recent in age.
misreadings: Could be read as the Ancient of Days opposite.

recorder-teachers.name: registradores-instructores
recorder-teachers.meaning: The sixth order of transition ministers: seraphim who record borderland transactions of the spiritual and the physical and teach techniques of fact recording (39:6.7, 48:6.30).

rejected.reason: 'Teachers' is 'Instructores' in the done terms; 'maestro' is reserved for 'Master'.

recorders.name: registradores
recorders.meaning: The beings who keep and forward the records of time and space, as on Uversa (25:6.4).

misreadings: Everyday sense: record clerks or recorder flutes.

rectangles-jerusem.name: rectángulos (Jerusem)
rectangles-jerusem.meaning: The one thousand areas of Jerusem occupied by the lower native life, with the headquarters of the spornagia at their center (46:7.1).

misreadings: Jerusem might be read as Jerusalem.

red-race.name: raza roja
red-race.meaning: The first of the six Sangik races, which went to the Americas (64:6.2).

second.name: raza roja
second.meaning: The first of the Sangik races of color, whose purer remnants crossed to North America about 85,000 years ago (64:6.5, 64:7.5).

misreadings: Everyday sense: Native Americans, a dated term.

reflectivator-liaisons-of-majeston.name: Enlaces Reflectivadores de Majeston
aliases: reflectivadores de enlace innominados de Majeston
reflectivator-liaisons-of-majeston.meaning: An unnamed group of beings connected with Majeston, listed among the Paradise classification and represented by the Reflective Image Aids (30:1.110, 15:10.21).

rejected.reason: 'reflectivo' is the form of 'Reflective'; 'Reflectivator' is a different coined word and needs its own form.
'reflector' reads as a lamp or mirror.

reflectivator-liaisons-of-majeston.note: The papers reveal almost nothing about this group. 15:10.21 inverts the words ('liaison reflectivators'), so the alias keeps that order.

second.name: Enlaces Reflectivadores de Majeston
second.meaning: An unrevealed, unclassified order listed in the Paradise classification of living beings next to Majeston of Paradise; nothing more is disclosed (30:1.110, 30:1.112).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; 'reflectivador' gives the coined word its own form apart from 'reflectivo'.

reflective-image-aids.name: Auxiliares de Imagen Reflectivos
reflective-image-aids.meaning: Forty-nine beings created by the Reflective Spirits, seven on each superuniverse headquarters, true images of their Spirit ancestors minus reflectivity, who serve as their channel of communication (17:4.1, 15:10.2).

rejected.reason: 'Aids' is 'Auxiliares' in 'Auxiliares Personales'; and 'Reflectiva' ties the adjective to the image only.

forcedChoices: 'Reflectivos' agrees with 'Auxiliares': Spanish forces the adjective onto one noun; it marks the order as that of the Reflective Spirits, since the Aids themselves lack reflectivity (17:4.1).

second.name: Auxiliares Reflectivos de Imagen
second.meaning: Forty-nine beings created by the Reflective Spirits, seven on each superuniverse headquarters, true images of their Spirit ancestors without reflectivity, who are the channel between the Reflective Spirits and the superuniverse authorities (17:4.1, 17:3.4).

adjudicated.reason: 17:4.1: the Image Aids of the Reflective Spirits. The form keeps the fixed 'Auxiliares de Imagen' together and uses 'Reflectivos' as in 'Espíritus Reflectivos'. Rejected: 'Auxiliares Reflectivos de Imagen' (splits the fixed term).

reflective-mother-spirits.name: Espíritus Madre Reflectivos
reflective-mother-spirits.meaning: The Reflective Spirits in their role as mothers of the Reflective Image Aids and the seconaphim (Paper 17, Paper 28).

rejected.reason: 'Reflexivo' means 'thoughtful'; see Reflective Spirits.

second.name: Espíritus Madre Reflectivos
second.meaning: The Reflective Spirits named as mothers of the Reflective Image Aids, who are their near duplicates minus reflectivity (17:4.1).

misreadings: Religious sense: Holy Spirit as mother.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it follows 'Espíritus Reflectivos' and avoids 'reflexivo' (thoughtful).

reflective-spirits.name: Espíritus Reflectivos
reflective-spirits.meaning: Forty-nine Spirits of Trinity origin on the superuniverse capitals, seven of each Master Spirit type, who operate universe reflectivity and are the mothers of the seconaphim (28:0, 40:10.2, 13:1.10).

rejected.reason: 'Reflexivo' means 'thoughtful' or grammatical 'reflexive'; the term names the reflection (reflectivity) of images and information, not thought.
'Reflector' reads as a device (a spotlight, a mirror) rather than a quality.

second.name: Espíritus Reflectivos
second.meaning: Forty-nine Trinity-origin beings, seven on each superuniverse capital, each a perfect reflection of one Master Spirit; they carry out reflectivity and are the mothers of the seconaphim (25:2.2, 17:8.2, 116:4.4).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; 'reflectivo' names reflectivity, while 'reflexivo' means thoughtful and 'reflector' reads as a device.

reflectivity.name: reflectividad
reflectivity.meaning: The power of the Infinite Spirit, working through the Reflective Spirits, to make the events and conditions of the universes known at once on the superuniverse headquarters; a secret of Spiritington (9:7, 13:1.10, 17:4.1).

rejected.reason: Means thought or mirror reflection; loses the coined '-ivity' term.
Spanish 'reflectividad' is a physics word for reflectance; the reader must not bring it.

backcheck.reading: The ability to reflect, either as a mirror or as thought.
backcheck.note: The power to reflect is a fair first guess.

second.name: reflectividad
second.meaning: Reflectivity is the Infinite Spirit's universe-wide faculty, working through the Reflective Spirits and Majeston, by which all mental, material and spiritual events are known at once to the universe rulers (17:2.2).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree, and it follows 'Reflective Spirits: Espíritus Reflectivos'.

reformation.name: Reforma
reformation.meaning: The fifteenth-century disruption of the unity of Christianity in Europe (92:5.15); elsewhere the papers use 'reformation' as a common noun for any reform (98:2.5, 196:2.1).

rejected.reason: The common noun for 98:2.5 and 196:2.1; the capital marks the historical movement.

reformation.note: Same entity as protestant-reformation. Translators must use lowercase 'reforma' for the common uses in 98:2.5, 99:7.1, and 196:2.1.

second.name: Reforma
second.meaning: The disruption of the unity of Christianity in Europe in the fifteenth century, caused by the inelasticity of institutionalized Christianity (92:5.15); the paragraph does not use the word 'Reformation'.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators and the judge agree; the capital marks the historical movement, and lowercase 'reforma' stays for the common uses (98:2.5, 196:2.1).

refuge.name: Refugio
refuge.meaning: The Buddhist profession of faith: «I take my refuge in the Buddha; in the Doctrine; in the Brotherhood» (94:8.1).

religion.name: religión

rejected.reason: Means ritual worship or a sect; the papers contrast religion with mere ritual and dogma.

second.name: religión
second.meaning: A living personal experience of spiritual communion with God that acts and bears fruit, as distinct from belief, tradition, or philosophy (102:2.8, 160:5.3, 5:4.7, 102:5.3).

religious-guardians.name: guardianes religiosos
religious-guardians.meaning: Master seraphim of planetary supervision, the 'angels of the churches', who keep values safe from one epoch to the next (114:6.7).

rejected.reason: The English adjective qualifies the guardians, not their object.

religious-leaders-in-rome.name: líderes religiosos de Roma
religious-leaders-in-rome.meaning: The Stoic, Cynic, and mystery-cult leaders in Rome whom Jesus taught for almost six months, preparing them for the later gospel (132:0.4).

rejected.reason: Also correct; "líderes" is more common in all regions.

remembrance-supper.name: Cena del Recuerdo
remembrance-supper.meaning: The supper Jesus established at the Last Supper, without ecclesiastical sanction, as the believer's symbolic meeting with Michael, in which the Master is really present (179:5.6, 179:5.8).

rejected.reason: A church term; the papers say the supper had no ecclesiastical sanction.
Good sense, but loses the plain word 'remembrance'.

second.name: Cena del Recuerdo
second.meaning: The supper Jesus established in the upper room as the symbol of the new dispensation, a symbolic rendezvous of the believer with Michael, without ecclesiastical sanction (179:5.2, 179:5.6, 179:5.8).

misreadings: Religious sense: the Last Supper or Eucharist.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it keeps the plain word 'remembrance' and avoids the church term 'Eucaristía', which the papers set aside (179:5.6).

remona.name: Remona
remona.meaning: Cain's distant cousin and wife, mother of Enoch, the head of the Elamite Nodites (76:2.9).

repersonalization.name: repersonalización
repersonalization.meaning: The reassembly of a surviving mortal on a mansion world: the soul in the morontia form, rejoined by the Adjuster, with memory, insight, and consciousness restored (49:6.9, 112:5.19).

rejected.reason: A separate word in the papers.
A different doctrine that the papers do not teach.

backcheck.reading: Giving a person their personality again after death.
backcheck.note: Personality given again after death fits.

reserve-corps.name: cuerpo de reserva
reserve-corps.meaning: Vast reserves of beings mobilized on Uversa, Salvington, and other capitals, sent on active service at the request of their group directors (30:3.10); also the mortal reserve corps of destiny (114:7.9).

reserve-corps-of-destiny.name: cuerpo de reserva del destino
reserve-corps-of-destiny.meaning: Groups of living mortals held in reserve to serve the superhuman government of a world in emergencies; Urantia has twelve such corps (114:7.7, 114:7.9).

rejected.reason: replaced by a human decision

decision.note: Consistency review 2026-10-21. Not yet checked by a Spanish speaker.

reservists.name: reservistas
reservists.meaning: Mortals of the reserve corps of destiny, little known to their fellows, who act in emergencies to prevent the breakdown of culture or the extinction of truth (114:7.9, 114:7.7).
reservists.note: Spanish 'reservista' first means a military reservist; the context gives the special sense.

second.name: reservistas
second.meaning: The mortal members of the reserve corps of destiny, chosen as protectors of planetary destiny, mostly unconscious of their role, who conserve essential planetary information (114:7.2, 114:7.10).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; the English uses the same military figure, and the context of the reserve corps of destiny gives the special sense.

resident-governors-general.name: gobernadores generales residentes
resident-governors-general.meaning: The representatives of the twenty-four Jerusem counselors who co-ordinate superhuman administration on Urantia, without personal authority of their own (114:3.2, 114:6.2).

resurrection.name: resurrección
resurrection.meaning: The reassembly of the survivor on the mansion worlds, when the soul and the returning Adjuster are united in a morontia form; also Jesus' morontia resurrection (30:4.11, 47:3, 189:1).

resurrection-halls.name: salas de resurrección
resurrection-halls.meaning: The halls on the mansion worlds and other receiving worlds where sleeping survivors are repersonalized in morontia form.

rejected.reason: 'Hall' here is a large room, not a corridor.

second.name: salas de resurrección
second.meaning: The seven radial wings of the Temple of New Life on the first mansion world where sleeping survivors are reassembled as conscious personalities (47:3.5, 189:3.2).

revelation.name: revelación
revelation.meaning: The disclosure of truth from above that supplements and corrects evolutionary religion, given in epochs and as personal religious experience (92:4, 101:2).

rejected.reason: Name of the Bible book (Revelations, Book of), not the concept.

backcheck.reading: Revelation, the uncovering of hidden truth by God.

revelations-book-of.name: Apocalipsis, libro del

rejected.reason: Literal, but Spanish readers do not know the book by this name.

revelations-book-of.note: The standard name 'Apocalipsis' loses the English link between 'Book of Revelation' and 'a great revelation' in 139:4.14. In common speech 'apocalipsis' also means a catastrophe; the reader must not bring that sense to the title.

second.name: Apocalipsis, libro del
second.meaning: The book John wrote on Patmos, preserved only in abridged and distorted form, with fragments of a great revelation (139:4.14).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it is the only name by which Spanish readers know the book. 'Libro de la Revelación' and 'Revelaciones' are not known names.

reversion.name: reversión
reversion.meaning: A return to past memories for relaxation and humor, promoted by the Reversion Directors in the morontia and spirit careers (30:3.7).

rejected.reason: Reads as hypnotic regression or a step backward in growth.

reversion.note: 'Reversión' in common Spanish is a legal return of property or a reversal; the reader must not bring those senses.

backcheck.reading: Reversion, a return to an earlier state.
backcheck.note: A return to an earlier state is a fair first guess for a return to memories.

second.name: reversión
second.meaning: A return to past memories, for relaxation and humor, that the Reversion Directors promote during the morontia transition (30:3.7, 48:3.11).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree, and it keeps the link with 'directores de reversión'.

reversion-directors.name: directores de reversión
