second.name: directores de reversión
second.meaning: Ministers of change and relaxation, the exalted humorists of the morontia and spirit realms, who have their assembly hall on Jerusem (48:4.3, 46:5.30, 48:3.11).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; 'reversión' keeps the coined word (a return), and 'regresión' brings a psychological sense.

rhine-river.name: río Rin
rhine-river.meaning: The river on which the Nordic-Danish and Danubian-Andonite cultures met and mingled (80:9.3).

rhodes.name: Rodas
rhodes.meaning: The Greek island where Jesus and his companions stopped on the voyage from Ephesus to Cyprus (130:0.3, 133:7.1).

misreadings: Could be the island or a surname.

rhythm-recorders.name: registradores del ritmo
rhythm-recorders.meaning: Thought recorders whom Urantians would call poets; they do many functions in rhythmic form for efficiency and pleasure (44:4.11).

rejected.reason: Suggests they record in rhythm, not that they work with rhythm.

rich-man-and-beggar.name: hombre rico y mendigo
aliases: el hombre rico y el mendigo
rich-man-and-beggar.meaning: An older Nazarite allegory, told by John the Baptist and recalled by Simon Peter, that warns those who love riches and covet dishonest wealth; it is not according to the new gospel (169:3.1).

rejected.reason: A traditional title from outside the text; it adds names the English does not give here.
'Pordiosero' is less neutral across countries than 'mendigo'.

backcheck.reading: The parable of the rich man and the beggar Lazarus.
backcheck.note: The reader names the story, as meant.

rich-man-of-rome.name: hombre rico de Roma
rich-man-of-rome.meaning: A wealthy Roman citizen and Stoic whom Jesus counseled to administer wealth as a wise trustee for later generations (132:5.1).

rich-widow-of-tyre.name: viuda rica de Tiro
rich-widow-of-tyre.meaning: A wealthy widow who followed Jesus through Galilee offering ever more money for healing, with no interest in the gospel (149:1.9).

rich-young-ruler.name: joven rico
rich-young-ruler.meaning: Matadormus, a rich young member of the Sanhedrin who asked Jesus about eternal life (163:2.4, 163:3.1).

rejected.reason: Heavy, and 'gobernante' suggests a head of state.

rich-young-ruler.note: The form drops 'ruler'. The papers call him 'rich young man'; he was a member of the Sanhedrin.

second.name: joven dirigente rico
second.meaning: Matadormus, the rich young member of the Sanhedrin who asked Jesus about eternal life and left when told to give his wealth to the poor (163:2.4, 163:3.1, 163:3.3); the papers say 'rich young man'.

misreadings: Religious sense: the rich young ruler in the Gospels.
backcheck.note: Standard Spanish name of the Gospel figure.

adjudicated.reason: 163:2.4 and 163:3.1: Matadormus, a rich young member of the Sanhedrin; the papers call him the 'rich young man'. Rejected: 'joven dirigente rico' (awkward, and adds a word the papers do not use for him).

rig-veda.name: Rig-Veda
rig-veda.meaning: The oldest of the Vedas, a compilation of sacred writings made by the Brahmans to combat the Salem teachers; it contains some of the highest and lowest deity concepts (94:1.7, 96:0.1, 111:0.7).

rejected.reason: Also correct in Spanish; the hyphenated form keeps the English spelling that the papers use.

backcheck.reading: The Rig Veda, Hindu sacred text.

right-hand-of-the-father.name: diestra del Padre
right-hand-of-the-father.meaning: The place of honor beside the Father, to which a Creator Son goes after each bestowal and where he receives sovereignty (20:4, 21:4, 189:3).

rejected.reason: 'Mano derecha' also means a trusted helper.

backcheck.reading: The right hand of the Father, the place of honor next to God.
backcheck.note: The place of honor next to God fits.

rimmon.name: Rimón
rimmon.meaning: A small city of Galilee once dedicated to Ramman, where Jesus and the twenty-four preached on the first tour (146:1.1, 146:0.1).

road-of-robbers.name: camino de los salteadores
road-of-robbers.meaning: The road up from Jericho to Bethany, called the "road of robbers", that Jesus took to the Passover (171:6.4); Barabbas was taken for robbery and murder on the Jericho road (185:5.3).

rejected.reason: 'ladrones' is taken by 'thieves' (ladrones crucificados con Jesús).
'bandido' is broader (outlaw); 'salteador' is a robber on the road.

road-of-robbers.note: 'salteador' is a little literary in some regions.

second.name: camino de los ladrones
second.meaning: The road up from Jericho to Bethany that Jesus and his party took to the Passover at Jerusalem, so called for its robbers (171:6.4).

misreadings: Religious sense: the road of the Good Samaritan.

adjudicated.reason: 171:6.4: the road from Jericho to Bethany, named for the robbers who attacked travelers there. 'Salteador' is a highway robber. Rejected: 'camino de los ladrones' ('ladrones' is a general thief, and collides with 'ladrones crucificados con Jesús').

rocky-mountains.name: Montañas Rocosas
rocky-mountains.meaning: The mountain range of western North America.

rodan-of-alexandria.name: Rodan de Alejandría
rodan-of-alexandria.meaning: A Greek philosopher of Alexandria, taught Jesus' teachings by a former apostle of John, who discussed philosophy with Nathaniel and Thomas at Magadan (161:0.2).

rejected.reason: The name exists only in this book; the English spelling stays.

roll-call.name: pase de lista
roll-call.meaning: The dispensational call of the names of the sleeping survivors (mercy) and of nonsurvivors (justice) at the resurrections (113:6.8, 45:4.1).

rejected.reason: Reads as a telephone call.

backcheck.reading: A roll call, a reading of names to check who is present.

roman-catholic-church.name: Iglesia católica romana
roman-catholic-church.meaning: The Roman church that grew from early Christianity, whose medieval control helped cause the secular revolt (entity record roman-catholic-church; see 195:8.6).
roman-catholic-church.note: A full-text search for 'Catholic church' gives no result. The entity aliases 'world religion' and 'one religion' do not look like names of this church; a human must check them.

second.name: Iglesia Católica Romana
second.meaning: The institutionalized Christian church of the West, which the papers describe as the totalitarian medieval church that mothered secularism and as a great world religion shaped by the continence cult (195:8.2, 89:3.6).

adjudicated.reason: The name is standard. A full-text search for 'Catholic' gives no result, and the aliases 'religión mundial' and 'una sola religión' are not names of this church, so I remove them to prevent false matches.

roman-centurion-in-corinth.name: centurión romano de Corinto
roman-centurion-in-corinth.meaning: A Roman centurion in Corinth whom Jesus told that sincere service of God and loyal service of Caesar do not conflict (133:4.3).

roman-centurion-of-jerusalem.name: centurión romano de Jerusalén
roman-centurion-of-jerusalem.meaning: The Roman officer at the crucifixion who, when he saw how Jesus died, said he must have been a Son of God and began to believe (187:5.5, 183:5.1).

misreadings: Religious sense: the centurion at the cross.
backcheck.note: Centurion at the cross is correct.

roman-empire.name: Imperio romano
roman-empire.meaning: The Roman Empire of Jesus' time and after (195:3.1).

second.name: Imperio romano
second.meaning: The empire whose provinces, under Herod's friendly relations with Rome, became safe for Jewish travel and later adopted Christianity (121:2.10, 195:3.1).

roman-judge-in-corinth.name: juez romano de Corinto
roman-judge-in-corinth.meaning: A Roman judge in Corinth whom Jesus told to judge justly and mercifully, as he too will come to judgment (133:4.7).

roman-magistrate-in-rome.name: magistrado romano en Roma
roman-magistrate-in-rome.meaning: The Roman magistrate (also called 'the judge') before whom Jesus defended a falsely accused poor man; he reopened the case and discharged the prisoner (132:4.8).

rejected.reason: The English says 'in Rome'; 'en Roma' matches 'soldados romanos en Jerusalén' already done.

roman-senator.name: senador romano
roman-senator.meaning: A Roman senator with whom Jesus talked on politics and statesmanship, and who then spent his life vainly urging that the people support the government, not the reverse (132:4.5).

roman-soldier-in-rome.name: soldado romano en Roma
roman-soldier-in-rome.meaning: A Roman soldier to whom Jesus spoke as they walked along the Tiber, urging courage, justice with mercy, and wholehearted reaching out for God as Father (132:4.6).

roman-soldiers-in-jerusalem.name: soldados romanos en Jerusalén
roman-soldiers-in-jerusalem.meaning: The Roman soldiers at Jerusalem, among them those who saw the stone roll from the tomb and fled to the fortress of Antonia (189:2.4).

romans.name: romanos
romans.meaning: The people of Rome, by nature and training lawyers who revered law (195:2.6).

rome.name: Roma
rome.meaning: The capital of the Roman Empire, a city of two million where Jesus spent time on his Mediterranean journey (132:0.2).

romulus.name: Rómulo
romulus.meaning: The legendary founder of Rome, named among those exposed as infants whose survival was credited to the gods (89:7.3).

round-heads.name: cabezas redondas
round-heads.meaning: The round-headed Andonites who, with the blue man, controlled central Europe for a time, mainly in the Danube valley (80:5.8).

rejected.reason: A technical anthropometric term; the English uses a plain descriptive word.
Capitalized, it names the Puritan party of the English Civil War (Roundheads); the papers use a plain lowercase description.

round-heads.note: The papers use the adjective 'round-headed' (80:5.8). In a sentence, 'andonitas de cabeza redonda' reads better than the noun form.

second.name: cabezas redondas
second.meaning: The round-headed Andonites who, with the blue man, controlled central Europe and the Danube valley about 5000 B.C. and were never fully displaced by the Andites (80:5.8).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; the lowercase plain description follows 80:5.8 and keeps it apart from the English Roundheads.

ruben.name: Rubén
ruben.meaning: One of the reputed tribes (with Gad and Gilead) that by tradition dwelt east of the Jordan, whose story Jesus told Joseph (128:1.14).

backcheck.reading: Reuben, a biblical tribe of Israel.

ruffians-at-nazareth.name: matones de Nazaret
ruffians-at-nazareth.meaning: The rough men, led by hirelings of Jesus' enemies, who seized Jesus at the Nazareth synagogue and tried to push him over a cliff (150:9.3).

rejected.reason: False friend: Spanish 'rufián' also means a pimp.
Implies habitual criminals, more than the English says.

second.name: matones de Nazaret
second.meaning: The hired rough men who seized Jesus in the Nazareth synagogue and rushed him to the cliff, but let him pass (150:9.3).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; 'rufián' is a false friend (also a pimp), and 'matones' gives rough, hired men (150:9.3).

rufus.name: Rufo
rufus.meaning: The son of Simon of Cyrene, whom Jesus and Ganid helped after an oxcart accident, and who later taught the gospel in Africa (130:6.6, 187:1.10).

misreadings: Religious sense: Rufus in Paul's letters.

runaway-lad-in-corinth.name: muchacho fugitivo en Corinto
runaway-lad-in-corinth.meaning: A young runaway in Corinth whom Jesus told that one cannot run away from God or oneself, and urged to face life bravely (133:4.11).

rejected.reason: 'Prófugo' implies flight from the law.
Less natural as a noun phrase.

runaway-lad-in-corinth.note: 128:7.8 also calls Jude, Jesus' brother, 'the runaway lad'. Translators must not link the two persons.

second.name: muchacho fugitivo de Corinto
second.meaning: A young man who had run away and whom Jesus counseled in Corinth that one cannot run away from God or from oneself (133:4.11); 128:7.8 uses the same phrase for Jude.

adjudicated.reason: 133:4.11: Jesus met the runaway in Corinth; the text does not say he came from there. Rejected: 'muchacho fugitivo de Corinto' (claims he was from Corinth).

russia.name: Rusia
russia.meaning: The present land named among places with Devonian red sandstone (59:4.7).

ruth-daughter-of-matthew.name: Rut (hija de Mateo)
ruth-daughter-of-matthew.meaning: Ruth, the eldest daughter of Matthew Levi, one of the ten women Jesus set apart for the ministering work of the kingdom (150:1.1).

ruth-old-testament.name: Rut (Antiguo Testamento)
ruth-old-testament.meaning: The biblical Ruth, named among the remarkable women in the ancestry of Mary, mother of Jesus (122:1.2).

ruth-sister-of-jesus.name: Rut (hermana de Jesús)
ruth-sister-of-jesus.meaning: Jesus' youngest sister, who married David Zebedee and went to Philadelphia (190:1.10).

ryonin.name: Ryonin
ryonin.meaning: A Japanese Buddhist teacher whose teachings, with those of Honen Shonin and Shinran, brought the God concept of Buddhism to the belief in Amida Buddha (94:12.2).

sabbath.name: sábado
sabbath.meaning: The seventh day of the week as a day of rest and worship, from its origin in Eden to its later Jewish rules (74:7, 147:6, 153:3).

rejected.reason: A loanword; plain Spanish names the day 'sábado'.
Descriptive phrase; loses the name of the day.

forcedChoices: lowercase 'sábado': Spanish writes days in lowercase; the English capital is the convention for a day name, not a coined term.
'sábado' is also the plain weekday Saturday: The context must show the day of rest; English 'Sabbath' is narrower than Spanish 'sábado'.

second.name: sábado
second.meaning: The seventh day of rest and worship, with its origin in the Eden custom of Adam, later bound by Jewish law; Jesus said it was made for man (74:4.6, 147:6.4).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; Spanish names the day of rest 'sábado', and the context gives the sense of rest and worship.

sacred-spheres-of-paradise.name: esferas sagradas del Paraíso
sacred-spheres-of-paradise.meaning: The three circuits of seven worlds each that circle Paradise inside Havona: the secret spheres of the Father, the luminous worlds of the Son, and the executive spheres of the Spirit (13:0.1-0.3).

rejected.reason: "santo" adds a sense of holiness of persons; the English says "sacred" and "spheres".

sadducees.name: saduceos
sadducees.meaning: The Jewish party of the priesthood and wealthy Jews who denied the resurrection and questioned Jesus in the temple (174:3.3).

sadib.name: Sadib
sadib.meaning: The second assistant Sovereign of the Satania system, number 271,402 of the tertiary order, who came to Satania with Lanaforge (45:3.4).

safed.name: Safed
safed.meaning: A town of Galilee where the apostles did personal work (138:9.3); home of James of Safed (158:4.2).

sage-of-salem.name: Sabio de Salem
sage-of-salem.meaning: Machiventa Melchizedek, known in Palestine as the sage of Salem (93:2.4, 51:3.9).

sagittarius.name: Sagitario
sagittarius.meaning: The dense star cloud that is the rotational center of our minor sector (15:3.5).

sahara.name: Sahara
sahara.meaning: The region of North Africa, once open grazing land of an indigo-black people, later the great Sahara desert (78:1.10, 80:1.4).

rejected.reason: Also accepted by the RAE, but less used in Latin America.

saharans.name: saharianos
saharans.meaning: The people of the Sahara when it was open land, who met blue men, Nodites, and Adamites in the Mediterranean basin (78:1.11, 80:1.1).

rejected.reason: The name of a modern people of Western Sahara.

forcedChoices: Lowercase, as Spanish writes names of peoples.

sakyamuni-buddha.name: Buda Sakyamuni
sakyamuni-buddha.meaning: A later title of Gautama, the Buddha (94:8.2), whose spirit some later followers said returned to earth as a 'living Buddha' (94:11.3).

rejected.reason: English word order; Spanish puts the title first, as in 'Buda, Sakyamuni' already done.

salamis.name: Salamina
salamis.meaning: The port on Cyprus from which Jesus and his companions sailed for Antioch (133:7.13).

salem.name: Salem
salem.meaning: The community of Melchizedek in Palestine, later Jebus and then Jerusalem, and the center of his teaching (93:2.4, 93:5.4).

misreadings: Religious sense: the city of Melchizedek.
Could also be the US town.

salem-teachings.name: enseñanzas de Salem
aliases: mandamientos de la religión de Salem
salem-teachings.meaning: The teaching of one God that Machiventa Melchizedek gave at Salem and that his missionaries spread (93:4.16, 95:3.5).

salome-sister-of-mary-mother-of-jesus.name: Salomé (hermana de María, madre de Jesús)
salome-sister-of-mary-mother-of-jesus.meaning: Mary's sister, to whom Mary confided that she thought her son would become a great teacher (122:3.3).

misreadings: Could be confused with Herod's stepdaughter.

salome-wife-of-zebedee.name: Salomé (esposa de Zebedeo)
salome-wife-of-zebedee.meaning: The wife of Zebedee and mother of the apostles James and John (Papers 125, 189).

salsatia.name: Salsatia
salsatia.meaning: The Census Director of Nebadon on Salvington, who is automatically aware of the birth and death of will in the local universe (37:8.4).

salvage-plan.name: plan de salvamento
salvage-plan.meaning: The plan that recovers creatures from sin and rebellion, which the authors think is a provisional feature of the bestowal plan of the Paradise Sons (186:5.8).

rejected.reason: Merges the term with 'salvation' (salvación), a separate word in the papers.
Reads mainly as the recovery of ships or goods at sea.

salvage-plan.note: 'Rescate' can also mean a ransom paid; the papers (186:5) reject the ransom idea of the bestowal, so a reviewer must confirm that the reader does not take that sense.

backcheck.reading: A plan to rescue or save someone.

second.name: plan de salvamento
second.meaning: The salvage plan is a provisional feature of the bestowal plan of the Paradise Sons, which sin and rebellion do not touch at its root (186:5.8).

adjudicated.reason: 186:5.8: the plan that recovers creatures from sin and rebellion. 'rescate' also means ransom, and 186:5 rejects the ransom idea of the atonement; 'salvamento' carries 'salvage' without it.

salvation.name: salvación
salvation.meaning: The free gift of God, received by faith, by which a person recognizes sonship with God and enters on eternal survival; it is not earned by works (150:5.3, 150:5.5, 193:1.2).

rejected.reason: Plain sense of physical rescue or ransom; changes the idea.
Brings a theology of payment for sin that the papers do not attach to the word.

second.name: salvación
second.meaning: The gift of the Father, revealed by his Sons and received by faith, which makes one a son or daughter of God (150:5.3, 150:5.2).

salvington.name: Salvington
salvington.meaning: The headquarters world of the local universe of Nebadon (32:2, 41:1.3).

misreadings: Could be read as a town named after salvation.

salvington-university.name: Universidad de Salvington
salvington-university.meaning: The Melchizedek university of Salvington, whose staff counts over one hundred thousand (20:8.2, 45:5.7).

rejected.reason: Done form of 'Melchizedek University'; this term keeps the place name.

second.name: Universidad de Salvington
second.meaning: The ten university clusters of forty-nine spheres each that surround Salvington, where man is spiritualized after constellation socialization (15:7.7).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it keeps the place name and stays apart from 'Universidad Melquisedec'.

samaria.name: Samaria
samaria.meaning: The region of Palestine between Judea and Galilee whose people the Jews avoided (124:6.1, 162:0.1).

samaritans.name: samaritanos
samaritans.meaning: The people of Samaria in central Palestine, long at enmity with the Jews.

samson.name: Sansón
samson.meaning: The biblical Samson, a life Nazarite and predecessor of John the Baptist in that vow (135:1.2; 140:5.16).

samuel.name: Samuel
samuel.meaning: The Hebrew prophet, a life Nazarite, whom the later record shows as crowning Saul (97:9.4, 135:1.2).

sanctities-of-service.name: Santidades del Servicio
sanctities-of-service.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim, the service indicators, who reveal the real nature and hidden motives of any service by man or angel (28:6.16, 28:6.19).

rejected.reason: Rare and abstract; not a natural word.

sanctities-of-service.note: 'Su Santidad' is the title of the pope; the reader must not bring that title to this order.

second.name: Santidades del Servicio
second.meaning: Tertiary seconaphim, the secoraphic service indicators, who reveal the true and hidden motives of any service by man or angel (28:6.16, 28:6.19).

misreadings: Religious sense: title of the Pope.
backcheck.note: Same figure as the English; context completes.

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it follows the English figure, and the context of the seconaphim (28:6.16) removes the papal title.

sandmatia.name: Sandmatia
sandmatia.meaning: A local system of the constellation of Norlatiadek, an immediate neighbor of Satania (41:2.1).

sangik-family.name: familia Sangik
sangik-family.meaning: The family of unusually intelligent children born suddenly to Badonite parents, the ancestors of all six colored races of Urantia (64:5.2, 64:7.1).

sangiks.name: Sangiks
sangiks.meaning: The six colored races, all descendants of the Sangik family that appeared among the highland Badonites (64:5.2, 64:6.17).

rejected.reason: Changes a name that exists only in this book.

sangiks.note: The Spanish plural of a word that ends in -k is not fixed. 'Sangiks' keeps the English; a reviewer can choose an invariable 'los Sangik'.

second.name: Sangiks
second.meaning: The six colored races that came from the nineteen children of the Sangik family, whose skins turned red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and indigo (64:5.3, 64:7.10).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it keeps a name that exists only in this book.

sanhedrin.name: Sanedrín
sanhedrin.meaning: The supreme Jewish council and court at Jerusalem that opposed Jesus and brought about his trial (184:0.1, 172:2.1).

second.name: Sanedrín
second.meaning: The high Jewish court and council at Jerusalem, which closed the synagogues to Jesus and later decreed his death (154:2.1, 168:3.3, 164:4.1).

sanobim.name: sanobines
sanobim.meaning: The energy-negative partner of the cherubim, the complement of being (38:7.2).

rejected.reason: the family plural follows serafines and querubines

second.name: sanobines
second.meaning: The negatively charged complement in the cherubim-sanobim pair, the left-hand deflector (38:7.2, 38:7.1).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; the plural follows 'serafines' and 'querubines', the family of the cherubim-sanobim pair (38:7.2).

sansa.name: Sansa
sansa.meaning: Daughter of Laotta (who died at her birth), reared by Eve with Cain; she married Sargan, chief of the northern blue races (76:0.2).

sanselon.name: Sanselon
sanselon.meaning: One of the nearest neighboring local universes of Nebadon in Orvonton (32:2.12).

sarah.name: Sara
sarah.meaning: The status wife of Abraham, mother of Isaac; brilliant and much younger than the Hebrew records say (93:9.3, 93:9.8).

rejected.reason: The standard Spanish form of the biblical name is 'Sara'.

sarepta.name: Sarepta
sarepta.meaning: A place on the Phoenician coast that Jesus and his company passed going south from Sidon to Tyre (156:3.2).
sarepta.note: The packet lists the type as 'being'; the papers show a place.

adjudicated.reason: The usual Spanish name of the Phoenician town (156:3.2); no doubt about the form.

sargan.name: Sargan
sargan.meaning: Chief of the northern blue races and husband of Sansa (76:0.2).

sargon-king-of-assyria.name: Sargón (rey de Asiria)
sargon-king-of-assyria.meaning: The king of Assyria who, about 700 B.C., took more than 25 000 Jews of the northern kingdom into captivity and put other peoples in their place, a source of the Jewish-Samaritan enmity (143:4.1).
sargon-king-of-assyria.note: The papers also name an earlier Sargon, the priest of Kish who made himself king in Mesopotamia (78:8.8). Keep the two apart.

adjudicated.reason: Standard Spanish form; the qualifier keeps him apart from Sargon of Kish (78:8.8).

sargon-priest-of-kish.name: Sargón (sacerdote de Kish)
sargon-priest-of-kish.meaning: The priest of Kish who proclaimed himself king, conquered Mesopotamia, and ended the priest-ruled city-states (78:8.8).

sarid.name: Sarid
sarid.meaning: A place near which Mary's brother had a farm, south of Nazareth on the Megiddo road, where the family fled an epidemic (123:1.7).

sartaba-mount.name: Sartaba (monte)
sartaba-mount.meaning: Mount Sartaba, above the Jordan valley, where Joseph and Mary stopped at noon (122:7.6).

sasta.name: Sasta
sasta.meaning: The name by which Gautama's followers called him, meaning master or teacher (94:8.2).

satan.name: Satanás
satan.meaning: A primary Lanonandek Son, Lucifer's first assistant, who represented the rebellion on Urantia (53:1, 53:5).

rejected.reason: Less common in neutral Spanish.
The reader must not bring the popular image of the devil as ruler of hell; in the papers Satan is a personal being of a defined order.

second.name: Satanás
second.meaning: A primary Lanonandek Son, first lieutenant of Lucifer, assigned to advocate the rebellion on Urantia; he never was a System Sovereign and is not the 'devil', who is Caligastia (53:1.4, 53:8.2).

adjudicated.reason: Both translators agree; it is the common form in neutral Spanish, and the papers define the person (53:1).

satania.name: Satania
satania.meaning: The local system of Urantia, with its capital on Jerusem, the site of the Lucifer rebellion (32:2.11, 53:0.1).

misreadings: Could be read as a place of Satan.

satania-power-center.name: Centro del Poder de Satania
satania-power-center.meaning: The Supreme Power Center of the sixth order at the gravity focus of Satania, on a dark island of space; with the Master Physical Controllers it lights, heats, waters, and energizes the 57 architectural worlds of Jerusem (41:1.5; 45:0.3).

rejected.reason: 'Power' is 'poder' in 'Centros Supremos del Poder'; 'energía' translates 'energy'.

satisfactions-of-service.name: Satisfacciones del Servicio
satisfactions-of-service.meaning: A group of secondary seconaphim attached to the Divine Counselors, who promote the value of unselfish service and the satisfactions that come from it (28:5.4).

sato.name: Sato
sato.meaning: A direct descendant of Adamson and Ratta who led the tall Adamsonite progenitors of the Greeks westward to Greece (80:7.3).

saturn.name: Saturno
saturn.meaning: The planet that, with Jupiter, formed from the massive central part of the matter pulled from the sun by Angona (57:5.9).

misreadings: Could be the planet or the Roman god.

saul-king.name: Saúl (rey)
saul-king.meaning: The first king of Israel, made king by the election of his troops after the defeat of the Ammonites, and defeated by the Philistines at Gilboa (97:9.4, 97:9.5, 97:9.13).

rejected.reason: Spanish uses Saulo for Paul of Tarsus; the king is Saúl.
